- `PortBoundary` says which side of a unit boundary a port is on. Its members are `GENERIC`, `INTERNAL` and `EXTERNAL`. A terminal's two ports are `INTERNAL` (panel side) and `EXTERNAL` (field cable side). A port's `pin_role` is an `elecdef.PinRole` or `None`: a contact's ports are `COMMON`, `BREAK` (closed at rest) or `MAKE` (closed when operated), a protective earth pin is `PE`.
- `Conductor` is a physical connection with exactly two ends. Its fields are `id`, `key`, `a`, `b`, `kind`, `carrier` (the item that carries it, or `None`) and `ext`. `a` and `b` are stored in id order, so they do not say a direction. The table is `conductors`.
- `ConductorKind` says what realises a conductor. Its members are `WIRE`, `CORE`, `JUMPER`, `BUSBAR`, `MOUNT`, `RAIL` and `LEAD`. `MOUNT`, `BUSBAR`, `RAIL` and `LEAD` are links: they close a net and are never wires.
- `PhysicalNet` is one net found from real connectivity: a maximal set of ports joined by conductors. Its only field is `ports`, sorted by id. It differs from a declared net, which is the intent the author wrote. Two closures over the same wiring compare equal.
- `NetClass` says what kind of potential or signal a `Net` carries. Its members are `POWER`, `CONTROL`, `SIGNAL`, `PE` and `GENERIC`. A 24 V supply rail is `POWER`; a 4-20 mA transmitter loop is `SIGNAL`. Read it as `net.net_class` on a row of `fr.derive.nets`.

## Lookups

- `aspect_nodes(model)` returns every `AspectNode`, keyed by id. It is the model's own table, not a copy, and it is empty when the model has none.
- `placements(model)` returns every `Placement`, keyed by id, in the same way.
- `boundaries(model)` returns every `Boundary`, keyed by id, in the same way.
- `conductors(model)` returns every `Conductor`, keyed by id, in the same way.
- `item_location(model, item)` returns the id of the `LOCATION` node the item is placed at. It uses the item's own placement, or the nearest placed ancestor's. It returns `None` when there is none. It raises `SchemaError` when `item` is not an item of the model.
- `items_at(model, node)` returns the ids of every item at `node` or at any node below it, once each and sorted by id. An item counts by its own placement, or by its nearest placed ancestor's. It raises `SchemaError` when `node` is not an aspect node of the model.
- `effective_placement(model, item, aspect)` returns the id of the `AspectNode` where `item` sits in `aspect`: its own placement, else its nearest placed ancestor's, else `None`. It walks `Item.parent` and stops on a cycle. A tie in one aspect resolves to the smallest placement id. It raises `SchemaError` when `item` is not an item of the model. Use it when you need one aspect's node; `item_location` is its `LOCATION` case.
- `subtree` takes a model and a node. It returns the ids of every descendant of `node`, following `parent`, with `node` itself left out. The result is sorted by id. It follows `parent` in any aspect and stops on a cycle. It raises `SchemaError` when `node` is not an aspect node.
- `net_of` takes a model and a port. It returns the `PhysicalNet` that contains the port. It returns `None` when the port is not a port of the model.
- `revision_history` takes a model and an optional release. It returns the `Revision` records of a release, in date order, then by version and revision as numbers, so revision 2 comes before revision 10. With `release=None` it returns the project's own history. It raises `SchemaError` when `release` is not `None` and is not a release of the model.

Use `item_location` when a list needs an item's place and the place may be inherited. Use `items_at` when you need everything in a cabinet or on a board, including the items under it.

## Id aliases

`fransys_model.derive` exports `UnitId`, `ItemId`, `FunctionId`, `PortId`, `DocumentId`, `NetId`, `ConductorId`, `AspectNodeId` and `UnitReleaseId`. Each is `Id[...]` of its record class. Annotate a value with the alias, so a module that only reads ids imports no record class. An output package reads sheets, documents and connector items through `DocumentRow`, `SheetRow`, `document_row`, `document_sheet`, `kind_sheet`, `schematic_page_ids` and `connector_item` of the same module, never through a record. `fr.derive` does not re-export them.

## Ratings and currents

- `fr.elecdef.Rating` says what a function or a part is rated for: `voltage`, `current` (each a tuple of `fr.elecdef.Range`, one per current kind in its `at`), `power_loss` and the other elecdef fields. A field is empty or `None` when the datasheet gives no value. A protective device's breaking figures are not in the `Rating`: they are the elecdef `Fuse` or `Breaker` of its `BlockFacet`. `fr.derive.Operating` holds `voltage`, `max_current` and `fault_current` as `Range` tuples and `fault_time_constant`, `capacity`, `resistance`, `nominal_power` and `nominal_current` as `Quantity`; read a figure with `.to(fr.elecdef.Unit.V).value`. The model checks the types only; comparing a rating with the plant is a check's job.
- `CurrentPosition` is one rated current path. Its fields are `functions` (sorted), `bounds` and `ports`. `bounds` holds at most one `CurrentBound` per current kind, AC before DC. `ports` are the two end ports of the path, and they tell apart paths that pass through the same functions, one per pole.
- `CurrentChain` is a block of the current graph. Its only field is `positions`, in the order that the chain lists them. The graph treats every switched link as closed. A position that exists only in some switch state is a chain on its own.
- `LimitRole` says what set a bound. Its members are `SOURCE`, a source's continuous limit, and `PROTECTION`, a full-range protective device.
- `port_potential_current` takes a model and a port. It returns the current kind, `AC` or `DC`, of the supply behind the port's potential. It returns `None` when the port has no potential rank, and it always returns `None` for protective earth, which belongs to no supply.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/keywords/index.md -->

# Keywords and handles

This page lists the public names of the facade's handles and signal types, then the keyword
arguments of the record constructors. The keywords of the `d.*` calls are in `keywords-design.md`,
those of the handle methods and layout hints in `keywords-handles.md`, those of the `fr.*` functions in `keywords-output.md`.

## Signal types and short names

A signal type says what kind of PLC channel or field signal a function asks for. The facade
gives the common ones short names. `fr.DI`, `fr.DO`, `fr.AI` and `fr.AO` are all members of
`fr.SignalType`, and each is passed as the `signal` of `plc`.

- `DI`: a digital input, `SignalType.DI`.
- `DO`: a digital output, `SignalType.DO`. `DO` belongs with `DI`, `AI` and `AO` as one of the four short names.
- `AI`: an analog input, the 4-20 mA current loop, `SignalType.AI_CURRENT`. Analog voltage inputs have no short name.
- `AO`: an analog output, the 4-20 mA current loop, `SignalType.AO_CURRENT`. Analog voltage outputs have no short name.

The short names cover only the current loops and the
two digital kinds. Use the full member, `fr.SignalType.<NAME>`, for the rest:

- `fr.SignalType.AI_VOLTAGE` and `fr.SignalType.AO_VOLTAGE`: analog voltage inputs and outputs.
- `fr.SignalType.RTD`: a resistance temperature detector, such as a Pt100.
- `fr.SignalType.RELAY`: a relay signal.

```python
import fransys as fr

assert fr.DI is fr.SignalType.DI
assert fr.AI is fr.SignalType.AI_CURRENT
rtd = fr.SignalType.RTD  # no short name; pass it as the `signal` of `plc`
```

## Handle types

Handles are the objects a design returns and the reader holds. A consumer does not build them.

- `Device`: one device, such as `Q1`. It reaches a function by name (`Q1.coil`) and a pin by brackets (`Q1[2]`). An unknown function or pin raises and lists the candidates. `Q1.tag` is the tag the call gave, or `None`.
- `Fn`: one function of a device, such as `K1.coil`. It reaches a pin by brackets (`Q1.main[2]`) or by name (`K1.coil.A1`). An unknown pin raises and lists the pins it has. `Fn.plc` requests a PLC channel.
- `Pin`: one port of one `Fn`. It has an `id`, an authoring `key`, a `name` that brackets match, and a `role`, such as `INTERNAL` or `EXTERNAL`.
- `Run`: a run of terminals on a strip, from `x1.run(...)`. It reaches a terminal by brackets (`run[1]`).
- `Cable`: one cable from `d.cable`. `w1.core(BN, a, b)` wires a core.
- `AcSupply`: what `d.ac_supply` returns. It holds the rails `L1`, `L2`, `L3` and `N` when it was given one.
- `DcSupply`: what `d.dc_supply` returns. It holds the rails `plus`, `minus` and `mid`.
- `SupplyRail`: one rail of a supply, such as `supply.L1` or `supply.plus`.
- `UnitDef`: what `@fr.unit` returns, the release of one unit. `d.add(definition, "U1")` builds it; a function that takes build arguments returns one.
- `Throw`: one throw of a changeover, `k1.co.no` or `k1.co.nc`. It stands in a `d.series` call as an element. A consumer does not build one (its `fns` are the changeover functions). A generated parts module declares it on every changeover function.
- `TypedDevice`: the base a generated parts module subclasses once for each part. Its `mpn` is its whole contract. It adds no behaviour: the subclass only declares functions and pins.
- `TypedFn`: the base a generated parts module subclasses for one function of one part. It adds no behaviour. Its subclass declares pins for the type checker.
- `BuildResult`: the result of `fr.build`. It holds `model`, the frozen and laid-out `Model`, `findings`, every finding collected while building it, and `settings`, the `Settings` the build used. `drawings` holds each schematic page's `Drawing`, with its placed `rows` (see `readability.md`). `page_svgs` holds each schematic page's SVG, drawn once and reused by `check` and `write`. `diagrams` holds the block-diagram sheets the document keeps, and is empty when it keeps none.
- `Settings`: the frozen value of `fr.settings(...)`, with the fields `paper`, `paper_by_kind`, `pdf`, `look` and `layout` (settings.md).
- `SettingsError`: raised by `fr.settings` for a file or `paper=` that is wrong. Its message names the file, the key and the keys known there.

## Type checking

A script written in this guide's spellings type-checks with no `ty: ignore` and no `Any`. Your ty settings need nothing.

- For full checking, generate a parts module (`fr.parts_module`, parts.md) and pass its classes to `d.device`. Each function and pin is a typed attribute, brackets take only the part's pin names, and a misspelt name is a type error.
- A device made from an MPN string is checked only at run time: a call on it checks nothing. Annotate it `fr.Device` to check the calls on it.
- On a `fr.Device`, a device-level pin by attribute (`q1.A1`) types as `fr.Fn` and is a ty error where a pin is needed. Write `q1["A1"]`; both run.
- Every handle in "Handle types" has a name on `fr`, so `fr.Device`, `fr.AcSupply` or `fr.UnitDef[Io]` annotates a parameter or a return.
- A function of a device is a `fr.Fn`: `k1.coil` and `q1.main` type as `fr.Fn`. A pin by brackets is a `fr.Pin`: `k1.coil["A2"]`, `q1["2"]` and `k1.coil.A1`. `k1.co.no` and `k1.co.nc` are changeover throws (`fr.Throw`); a generated changeover function declares both.
- A pin chosen by an `int` loop variable is a ty error against a typed part's pin names: loop over `fn.pins`. A computed name, `f"CH {n}"`, is a ty error too.
- A wrong function or pin name is a run-time error. It raises and lists the names the part has. A pin named `+` or `-` is the attribute `_plus` or `_minus`.
- A unit with build arguments is a factory that returns `fr.UnitDef` (units.md, "Variants and revised copies").

## Severity

`Severity` says how much a `Finding` blocks a downstream output. The facade alone decides which
severities block which outputs.

- `ERROR`: blocks every export. `write` raises and writes nothing while any error finding remains. There is no escape hatch.
- `WARNING`: worth a look. It blocks nothing under the facade's policy.
- `INFO`: worth noting. It blocks nothing under the facade's policy.

## Model and Finding

The facade builds these records. A consumer reads them and does not construct them. `freeze`
builds a `Model`, and the domain validators and the facade build the `Finding` values.

### Model

`Model` is the immutable, validated result of `freeze`. Everything reachable from it is deeply immutable, and `freeze` checks that.

- `schema_version`: the model schema number. `freeze` stamps the number this build knows. Reading data with a number this build does not know raises an error.
- `aliases`: a map from a retired id to the id that replaces it. `freeze` rewrites every reference to a retired id into one to its replacement. `Draft.alias` fills it.
- `origins`: a map from an id to its `Origin`, the file, line and note where the record was authored. It sits outside the tables. Moving a line does not change the digest.
- `digests`: one digest for each registered namespace, such as `core`, `facet` or `layout`. A change to `layout` records leaves the `core` and `facet` digests alone.
- `digest`: one digest that combines the `digests`. A generated parts module records it as its library digest. `fr.design` refuses a stale module, so a library change must be regenerated before use.
- `Model.origin_of` and `Model.key_of` read `origins` and the tables. See `target` below.

### Finding

`Finding` is one reported engineering problem. Every domain validator emits this one shape. All four fields are required keyword arguments.

- `code`: a stable `UPPER_SNAKE` string, such as `NET_UNREALISED`. The module that emits it lists it. The reader sees it in the findings list. The order is error, warning, then info, and inside each band by `code`, then `subjects`, then `message`.
- `severity`: a `Severity`. Only `ERROR` stops an export. See the Severity section above.
- `subjects`: the ids the finding is about. They are stored once each, in id order, so the order a validator found them in does not matter.
- `message`: the text a reader sees. For a `write` finding the facade's `describe` turns it into printed text first. A `release` finding prints its message as written.

## Draft calls

A `Draft` collects records from input files before `freeze`. Inputs call these methods. A consumer
rarely does.

- `origin` on `Draft.add` and `Draft.extend`: the `Origin` the records are attributed to. It is required, with no default. An identical record already present keeps the smaller origin by `(file, line, note)`, so call order does not matter. A different record under the same id raises a merge conflict. `extend` is not atomic: a conflict leaves the records before it in place.
- `old` on `Draft.alias`: the id that has been retired. The `new` argument is its replacement. It raises when `old` is `new`, the two are of different kinds, or `old` is already retired in favour of another id. The input decoder and the merge both call it.
- `target` on `Draft.key_of`, `Draft.origin_of` and `Draft.record_of`: the id to look up. `key_of` returns the record's authoring key, `origin_of` returns its `Origin`, and `record_of` returns the record itself. Each returns `None` when nothing is held. `record_of` does not follow an alias.
- `target` on `Model.key_of` and `Model.origin_of`: the same lookup on a frozen `Model`. `key_of` returns `None` when no record holds the id. `origin_of` returns the `Origin` or `None`. The `describe` function asks it where an id was written.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/keywords-design/index.md -->

# Keywords of the d calls

This page has one table for each `d.*` and `d.detail.*` call: each keyword, its default, its effect and an example.
A call that takes only `*args` has no table; one sentence says what it takes.

`place=` is the same on every call that takes it: see its table in `authoring.md`.
The `fr.*` functions are in `keywords-output.md`, the handle methods and layout hints in `keywords-handles.md`.

## `d.device`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | required | The printed tag, with no lowercase letter. `None` numbers the device from its class code and needs `name=`. | `d.device("Q1", P.Q)` |
| [`part`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/parts/index.md#the-typed-parts-module) | required | A part class or an MPN string. `None` makes an `external=True` box of `pins=`, with no BOM line. | `d.device("Q1", "DEMO-MCB-3P")` |
| [`pins`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `None` | Names the pins of a part-less box (`part=None`); each is an attribute too, `ext.U` as `ext["U"]`. | `d.device("A1", None, pins=("1", "2"), external=True)` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the device stands. | `d.device("Q1", P.Q, place="HOLD")` |
| [`parent`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/parts/index.md#an-accessory-in-its-holder) | `None` | The device, strip or cable that holds this one; an accessory prints its holder's designation. | `d.device("J1", P.HSG, parent=k1)` |
| `name` | `None` | The key a released number holds to. Needed when `tag=None`. | `d.device(None, P.Q, name="main-breaker")` |
| [`interface`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#the-interface) | `False` | Marks functions as the unit's boundary: `True` all, a tuple those. | `d.device("X1", P.CONN, interface=True)` |
| [`unused`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#the-interface) | `False` | Marks functions as unused, so no unused-pin finding is raised: `True` all, a tuple those. | `d.device("X1", P.CONN, unused=("x2",))` |
| `mounted_on` | `None` | Mounts the device on a carrier, as a contactor on a protective switch; the carrier's load pins join this device's line pins pole by pole. | `d.device("K1", P.CTR, mounted_on=q1)` |
| [`joins`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/harnesses/index.md#fit-a-housing-on-a-parts-leads) | `None` | Maps the housing's pins to the parent's pins, joined with no wire. Needs `parent=` to be a device. | `d.device("J1", P.HSG, parent=k1, joins={1: k1.coil["A1"]})` |
| `description` | `''` | Designation-list text in place of the part's description. | `d.device("Q1", P.Q, description="Pump breaker")` |
| `position` | `None` | The physical order within the parent, such as a PLC module's slot. | `d.device("A2", P.DI8, parent=rack, position=2)` |
| `installed` | `True` | `False` keeps the device in drawings but drops it from the BOM. | `d.device("Q9", P.Q, installed=False)` |
| [`external`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `False` | `True` marks the device as supplied by others: no BOM line, and drawings mark it dashed "(by others)". | `d.device("M1", P.MOTOR, external=True)` |
| [`contacts`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/harnesses/index.md#add-crimp-contacts) | `None` | Fits a contact part in every pin of a housing, or a pin-to-part mapping for mixed contacts. | `d.device("P1", P.HSG, parent=w1, contacts="DEMO-CRIMP-M")` |

## `d.terminal_strip`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | required | The printed tag. `None` numbers the strip and needs `name=`. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 10)` |
| `part` | required | The terminal part. `None` makes part-less terminals with only `.outer`; needs `external=True`. | `d.terminal_strip("X9", None, external=True)` |
| [`count`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#strips-and-terminals) | `None` | The number of terminals. `X1[3]` makes terminal 3 on first use. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, count=10)` |
| `name` | `None` | The key a released number holds to. Needed when `tag=None`. | `d.terminal_strip(None, P.TB, name="field")` |
| `description` | `''` | Designation-list text in place of the part's. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, description="Field strip")` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the strip stands. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, place="HOLD")` |
| [`pe`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#strips-and-terminals) | `None` | The part of the strip's protective-earth terminals. A run labelled `"PE"` takes it and raises without one. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")` |
| [`interface`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#strips-and-terminals) | `False` | Marks terminals as the unit's boundary: `True` all, a tuple those. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 4, interface=(1, 2))` |
| [`unused`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#strips-and-terminals) | `False` | Marks terminals as unused: `True` all, a tuple those. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 4, unused=(3, 4))` |
| [`bridged`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#bridges) | `False` | Bridges plain terminals: `True` bridges all, `(first, last)` a range, a tuple of ranges several. | `d.terminal_strip("X4", P.TB, 6, bridged=(2, 6))` |
| [`rail`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#power-rails) | `False` | Declares the strip's one bridged group a power rail; several ranges raise. | `d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 4, bridged=True, rail=True)` |
| [`external`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `False` | `True` flags the strip and its terminals as by others. | `d.terminal_strip("X9", P.TB, 4, external=True)` |

## `d.cable`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | required | The printed tag. `None` numbers the cable and needs `name=`. | `d.cable("W1", P.CBL)` |
| `part` | required | The cable part, which gives the cores. | `d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")` |
| `length_m` | `None` | The length in metres, stored as whole millimetres, printed in the cable list. | `d.cable("W1", P.CBL, length_m=5)` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the cable stands. | `d.cable("W1", P.CBL, place="HOLD")` |
| [`parent`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/series/index.md#cables) | `None` | The harness that holds the cable. | `d.cable("W5", P.CBL, parent=h1)` |
| `name` | `None` | The key a released number holds to. Needed when `tag=None`. | `d.cable(None, P.CBL, name="motor-cable")` |
| `external` | `False` | `True` flags the cable as supplied by others; its cores carry no flag. | `d.cable("W1", P.CBL, external=True)` |

## `d.add`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `definition` | required | The unit made by `fr.unit`. The call returns the unit function's result. | `u1 = d.add(board, "U1")` |
| `tag` | required | The instance's printed tag, with no lowercase letter. | `d.add(board, "U1")` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the instance stands. | `d.add(board, "U1", place="HOLD")` |
| `name` | `None` | The identity a released number holds to, when it must differ from the tag. | `d.add(board, "U1", name="module1")` |

## `d.unused`

`d.unused(*points)` takes typed boundary points of nested units, as `d.add` returned them (`pc.x3[3]`, a strip, a device or a function), or a port (`m1.minus`).
It declares them left open on purpose by this design. It has no keywords. A wired point, a point that is no boundary and a point
listed twice are refused; see `units.md`, which holds the worked example.

## `d.ac_supply`

`d.ac_supply(name, voltage, *phases, ...)` takes the phase pins in phase order as `phases`: one or three.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | The supply's name. Its rails are `ac.L1` and so on. | `d.ac_supply("230V", 230, x0[1], n=x0[2])` |
| [`voltage`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | required | Each phase's RMS voltage to the star point. | `d.ac_supply("400V", 400, q1["L1"], q1["L2"], q1["L3"])` |
| [`n`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | The neutral pin. A series joins N only where an element has a pole. | `n=q1["N"]` |
| [`names`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | Renames the potentials: one name per phase pin, then one for `n`. The rails keep their names. | `names=("A", "B", "C")` |

## `d.dc_supply`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | The supply's name. Its rails are `dc.plus` and `dc.minus`. | `d.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)` |
| [`source`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | A device or function whose L+ and L- pins and voltage are the supply. Without it, `plus`, `minus` and `voltage` are required. | `d.dc_supply("24VDC", g1.output)` |
| [`plus`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | The plus pin, with no `source`. | `plus=x1[1]` |
| [`minus`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | The minus pin, with no `source`. | `minus=x1[2]` |
| [`mid`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | A middle conductor at 0 V; plus and minus are then plus and minus the voltage. | `mid=x1[3]` |
| [`voltage`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | The voltage, required when no `source` or its part states none. | `voltage=24` |
| [`names`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#ac-or-dc-supply-and-rails) | `None` | Renames the potentials, in the order plus, minus, mid. | `names=("P24", "M24")` |

## `d.earth`

`d.earth(*pins)` takes the pins to join to protective earth, one `PE` net. A terminal lands on its inner side. Example: `d.earth(x1[3], q1["PE"])`.

## `d.function`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`name`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | required | The function block's name, printed `=name`. Devices made inside the `with` block belong to it, which sets their designation. | `with d.function("RUN", "Pump run"):` |
| [`text`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | required | The block's description, printed on the pages that draw it. | `with d.function("RUN", "Pump run"):` |

A function block that holds only a connection draws nothing of its own. Put the devices of that circuit in the block, and the circuit draws there.

## `d.location`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`name`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | required | The place's tag, printed `+name`. | `d.location("HOLD", "Engine hold")` |
| [`text`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | required | The place's description. | `d.location("HOLD", "Engine hold")` |
| [`within`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#a-place-inside-a-place) | `None` | The outer place, which must exist; the place prints `+outer+name`. `None` puts it at the root. | `d.location("BATT", "Batteries", within="HOLD")` |

## `d.harness`

Refused for 0.22 (`MATES_DISABLED`, an ERROR): draw the link as a cable or wires.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`tag`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/harnesses/index.md#add-a-harness) | `None` | The part-less harness's tag. `None` numbers it and needs `name=`. | `d.harness("H1")` |
| `name` | `None` | The key a released number holds to. | `d.harness(None, name="main-loom")` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the harness stands. `None` gives it no place. | `d.harness("H1", place=None)` |
| `external` | `False` | `True` flags the harness as by others. | `d.harness("H1", external=True)` |

## `d.rack`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | required | The part-less PLC rack's tag. Modules go under it with `parent=`. | `d.rack("U1")` |
| `name` | `None` | The key a released number holds to. | `d.rack("U1", name="plc")` |
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `...` | Where the rack stands. `None` gives it no place. | `d.rack("U1", place="HOLD")` |
| `external` | `False` | `True` flags the rack as by others. | `d.rack("U1", external=True)` |

## `d.mate`

Refused in 0.22 (`MATES_DISABLED`, an ERROR): draw the link as a cable or wires.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`a`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#plug-a-connector) | required | The connector to plug in: a one-function device, or that function. | `d.mate(j1, j2)` |
| [`b`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#plug-a-connector) | required | The connector `a` plugs into. | `d.mate(j1, j2)` |

## `d.series`

`d.series(*elements, ...)` takes the elements to wire end to end, each one's load to the next one's line. A pin or a tuple of one device's pins starts or ends it.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`wire`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/series/index.md#colour-by-what-a-wire-carries) | `None` | The wire of every pole: a size, a table of rows that replaces only those rows, one `(colour, size)`, or a tuple of them in pole order. `None` uses the rows' defaults; a row with no size is `WIRE_ROW_UNRESOLVED`. A series through a cable whose part has a core table needs no `wire=`. | `d.series(dc.plus, k1.aux, h1.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))`; `d.series(x1[1:4], q1.element, wire=((BN, 1.5), (BK, 1.5), (GY, 1.5)))` |

## `d.pair`

`d.pair(a, cable, b)` joins two ends through a cable pin for pin: core `i` runs from `a`'s pin `i` to `b`'s pin `i`, with no line or load direction.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`a`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#when-a-detail-call-is-right) | required | The first end: terminals (`x8[1:3]`; field side), a function (`b1.sig`, pins in connector order), or pins (`b1.sig[1]`), as `d.series` reads them. | `x8[1:3]` |
| [`cable`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#when-a-detail-call-is-right) | required | The cable between the ends. | `w3` |
| [`b`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#when-a-detail-call-is-right) | required | The second end, with as many pins as `a`; a strip or a device raises. Both ends need the same number of pins, or the call raises. | `b1.sig` |

Example: `d.pair(x8[1:3], w3, b1.sig)`.

## `d.parallel`

`d.parallel(*members)` takes the members to group, so a series puts each between the previous load and the next line. It connects nothing alone. Example: `d.series(dc.plus, d.parallel(h1.lamp, h2.lamp), dc.minus)`.

## `d.poles`

`d.poles(*functions, ...)` takes one-pole contacts of one device, in pole order, as one multi-pole element. A series wires the group.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`selector`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/series/index.md#contacts-that-switch-together) | `False` | `True` turns a changeover group's throws to the line side: a series enters at the throws, and the group draws turned. `False` keeps the line at the commons. It raises on a part that states a selector or a group that is not changeovers. | `q = d.poles(k1.co_1, k1.co_2, k1.co_3, selector=True)` |

## `d.project`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`title`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#title-block-revision) | required | The project title, printed in every title block. | `d.project(title="Pump", ...)` |
| [`number`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#title-block-revision) | required | The drawing number, printed in the title block. | `number="DC-1"` |
| [`customer`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#title-block-revision) | required | The customer, printed in the title block. | `customer="Demo Ltd"` |
| `revision` | required | The current revision, an integer from 1; its date is the matching `d.revision` entry's. | `revision=2` |
| [`author`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | required | The author, printed in the Author cell. | `author="AB"` |
| [`notice`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | `None` | Not accepted: passing it raises `AuthorError`. Use `fr.document(notice=)`. | `fr.document(preset, None, cover=c, notice="...")` |
| `version` | `1` | The project's release version, which `d.revision` entries take by default. Set it before any `d.revision`. | `version=2` |

## `d.revision`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`revision`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | The revision number of this history entry. | `d.revision(1, date="2026-01-01", text="first", created="AB")` |
| [`date`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | The entry's date, shown in the title block for the current revision. | `date="2026-01-01"` |
| [`text`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | What the revision changed. | `text="first issue"` |
| [`created`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | Who made the revision. | `created="AB"` |
| `checked` | `''` | Who checked it. | `checked="CD"` |
| `approved` | `''` | Who approved it. | `approved="EF"` |
| [`version`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | `None` | The entry's version. `None` takes the project's version, or 1 before `d.project`. | `version=2` |

## `d.draft`

`d.draft()` takes nothing. It returns the records written so far, without freezing or merging the library: `fr.build` does both.


## `d.detail.busbar`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`a`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#ddetailbusbar) | required | The first pin of the busbar. | `d.detail.busbar(x1[1], x1[2])` |
| [`b`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#ddetailbusbar) | required | The second pin. The same pin twice raises. | `d.detail.busbar(x1[1], x1[2])` |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/keywords-handles/index.md -->

# Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

This page has one table for each handle method and each `d.layout.*` hint: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example fragment.
A call that takes only `*args` has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.

The design calls are in `keywords-design.md`, the `fr.*` functions in `keywords-output.md`.
`d.layout.profile` keeps its table in `layout-numbers.md`.

## `Fn.plc`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`signal`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#how-channels-are-numbered) | `None` | Required on a device. The `fr.SignalType` of the PLC channel this function needs, such as `fr.DI`. It picks the channel kind allocated. A module's channel handle (`ai.ai_3`) already has its signal and takes none. | `k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run")` |
| [`name`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#request-a-plc-channel) | `None` | Required on a device. The channel's name. It prints in the PLC lists and on the channel's address, and is the channel's `Name` in the Wago rack XML. On a spare channel's handle it names the spare (`unused`). | `k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run")` |
| `priority` | `0` | A lower number is served first when channels are short. Ties go by the requesting function's key, then its id. | `k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run", priority=1)` |
| [`routing`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#the-wago-rack-xml-follows-the-cdp-reference) | `None` | The channel's CDP routing path, never parsed. `None` writes no `Routing`, `""` writes `Routing=""`, a path writes the path. | `k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run", routing="Controller.Section.Pump_run")` |
| [`configured`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#the-wago-rack-xml-follows-the-cdp-reference) | `True` | `False` on a module's channel handle leaves the channel out of the Wago rack XML; the other channels keep their `Nr`. It takes no name, routing or scale; a device refuses it. | `ai.ai_4.plc(configured=False)` |
| [`description`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#request-a-plc-channel) | `None` | One line of text for the PLC list, which prints it in its own column beside the signal name. It stays in the list: the drawing does not print it, and it never reaches the Wago rack XML, where the channel `Name` stays the bare name. A blank string or one with a line break raises. | `k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run", description="Start the main pump")` |

`fn.plc(...).scale(...)` sets a per-channel engineering range; see `Fn.scale`. On a spare analogue channel's handle, `scale` scales that channel.

## `Fn.pole`

`fn.pole(n)` takes one pole number, counted from 1 in pole order, and gives that one pole of the function as a series element: `d.series(s1.main.pole(2), f2.element, wire=(BK, 1.5))`.

A pin, or a tuple of one device's pins, is a series element anywhere. First, its pins are the load ends: `d.series(k1.coil["A1"], a1.di_1, wire=(BK, 1.0))` leaves from A1, where `d.series(k1.coil, a1.di_1)` leaves from A2. Last, they are the line ends. In the middle a pin is both: it takes as many pins as its neighbours have poles.

`fn.pins` is the function's pins as a typed tuple in the connector list's order (`1, 2, 10, A1`): `a.pins[i]` is the i-th pin from 0, and a loop over it types as `fr.Pin`.

## `Fn.scale`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`unit`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#request-a-plc-channel) | `None` | The engineering unit of the scaled value. It prints in the Wago rack XML only, not in the PLC list. `None` writes no `Unit`; `""` raises. | `ai.scale("bar", raw=(0, 27648), eng=("0", "10"))` |
| [`raw`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#request-a-plc-channel) | required | The raw range as two integers. | `raw=(0, 27648)` |
| [`eng`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#request-a-plc-channel) | required | The engineering range as two strings or Decimals. Floats are refused. | `eng=("0", "10")` |

## `TerminalStrip.run`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`label`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#bridges) | required | The run's label. It prints on each terminal of the run. A run labelled `"PE"` takes the strip's `pe=` part. | `x1.run("24V", 4)` |
| [`count`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#bridges) | `None` | The number of terminals in the run. With none, the run is bridged and grows as it is used. | `x1.run("24V", 4)` |
| [`bridged`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#bridges) | `False` | Bridges the run's terminals with jumpers: `True` bridges all, `(first, last)` bridges a range. | `x1.run("24V", 4, bridged=True)` |
| [`rail`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#power-rails) | `False` | Declares the bridged run a power rail: its terminals draw as the rail's power symbol, not as terminals. A run of one terminal is allowed. A fused terminal in the group is `RAIL_ON_FUSED`: flag the supply side of the fuse. | `x1.run("24V", 4, bridged=True, rail=True)` |
| [`interface`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#the-interface) | `False` | Marks the run's terminals as the unit's boundary: `True` marks all, a tuple of terminal numbers marks those. | `x1.run("24V", 4, interface=True)` |
| [`unused`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#the-interface) | `False` | Marks the run's terminals as unused: `True` marks all, a tuple marks those. | `x1.run("SPARE", 2, unused=True)` |

`TerminalStrip.label` is the strip's label as the design printed it (`"X5"`); `Run.label` is the run's own label (`"PE"`). Both are read-only.

## `Cable.core`

Use `d.series` through the cable first: it takes the next free core. Use `core` to choose one core.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`which`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#w1core) | required | The core, by colour or by 1-based number. | `w1.core(BN, a, b)` |
| [`a`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#w1core) | required | The first pin of the core. With no `b`, the core is a shield core, refused for now (`SCREEN_DISABLED`). | `w1.core(1, x1[1], m1["U"])` |
| [`b`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/detail/index.md#w1core) | `None` | The second pin of the core. `None` is for a shield core only, which is refused for now. | `w1.core(BN, x1[1], m1["U"])` |

## `Cable.spare`

`Cable.spare(*cores, ...)` takes the cores to mark spare, by colour or number. With none, it marks every core not wired or marked so far, so wire first.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | `None` | A pin that parks one spare core. `None` leaves it unparked. An `SH` core refuses it: use `core(which, a)`. | `w1.spare(BK, at=x1[9])` |

## `d.layout.order`

`d.layout.order(*groups)` takes function groups: each neighbour pair is drawn in this order. It has no named keyword. A name that is not a group handle raises `AuthorError`. Example: `with d.function("PUMPS", "Pumps") as pumps: ...`, then `d.layout.order(pumps, valves)`.

## Keywords a consumer never passes

- `engine` on `Layout`: the design's engine. `d.layout` builds the layout around it, so you never pass it.
- `pe_mpn` on `TerminalStrip`: the strip's PE terminal part. Pass `pe=` to `d.terminal_strip` instead.
- `rail_group` on `TerminalStrip`: the design's rail declaration. Pass `rail=True` to `run` or `d.terminal_strip` instead.

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/keywords-output/index.md -->

# Keywords of the fr functions

This page has one table for each `fr.*` function: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example call fragment.
A call that takes only `*args` has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.

The tier of each call is the first word of its docstring (index.md, Tiers).
The design calls are in `keywords-design.md`, the handle methods and layout hints in `keywords-handles.md`.

## `fr.design`

`fr.design(*libraries, ...)` takes the part libraries or generated parts modules as `libraries`.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`place`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/authoring/index.md#name-a-place-and-a-function-block) | `None` | Names the first location as a bare tag. With `None` the design has no location until you call `d.location`. | `fr.design("demo_parts", place="C1")` |
| [`wiring`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/series/index.md#colour-by-what-a-wire-carries) | `None` | Replaces the default wire colour and size of the rows it names, for this design. Rows not named keep the IEC 60204-1 default. | `fr.design("demo_parts", wiring={fr.DC_SUPPLY: (BU, 1.5)})` |

## `fr.unit`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | The unit release name. Instances print it, and the release folder under `fr.release` carries it. | `@fr.unit("pump-board", revision=2, ...)` |
| [`revision`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | The current revision. It is the last entry of the unit's history. | `revision=2` |
| `interface_version` | required | The unit's boundary version. You bump it by hand when the interface changes. | `interface_version=1` |
| [`date`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | Date of the current revision, as written in its history entry. | `date="2026-01-01"` |
| [`text`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | What the current revision changed, as written in its history entry. | `text="added the fuse"` |
| [`by`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | required | Who made the current revision. It prints in the history as `created`. | `by="AB"` |
| [`version`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | `1` | The release version. Revisions count within a version, and `fr.release` names the folder `<version>.<revision>`. | `version=2` |
| `title` | `''` | The unit's own title-block title. Empty gives a `TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING` warning on its document. | `title="Pump board"` |
| `number` | `''` | The unit's own title-block number. Empty gives a `TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING` warning on its document. | `number="DWG-101"` |
| [`history`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#recording-revisions) | `()` | Earlier revisions of the unit. Each entry is a mapping of the `d.revision` keywords `revision`, `date`, `text` and `created`. | `history=[{"revision": 1, "date": "2025-12-01", "text": "first", "created": "AB"}]` |

## `fr.document`

`fr.document(preset, subject, ...)` takes the preset and the subject as positional arguments.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`preset`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | required | The `fr.DocumentPreset` that fixes the deliverable's default page kinds (documents.md). | `fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.SYSTEM, None, cover=Path("cover.md"))` |
| [`subject`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#subjects) | required | What the document is about: what `d.location(...)` returns, a `Device`, a unit release name, or `None` for the system preset. Another value raises `TypeError`. | `fr.document(preset, "pump-board", cover=cover)` |
| [`cover`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | required | The Markdown cover file, stored verbatim. Its stem is the document's key. A missing file raises `FileNotFoundError`. A `<stem>.notes.md` beside it becomes the notes page. | `cover=Path("cover.md")` |
| [`logo`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | `None` | An SVG file for the title block's logo cell. `None` leaves the cell empty. A missing file raises. | `logo=Path("logo.svg")` |
| [`notice`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/documents/index.md#presets-cover-and-notes-text) | `''` | The title block's IP notice text, printed on every page of this document. Empty leaves the cell empty. | `notice="Property of Demo Ltd"` |

## `fr.readability`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The `BuildResult` to measure. It reads the drawings and the block-diagram layout (`BuildResult.diagrams`) the build kept and lays nothing out again; the call returns one row per drawn page, each naming its unit. | `fr.readability(result)` |

## `fr.settings`

`fr.settings(path=None, *, paper=None)` returns a `fr.Settings`: our defaults, the consumer's TOML file on top, and `paper` per drawing type (settings.md).

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`path`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/settings/index.md#the-toml-file) | `None` | The consumer's TOML file, merged key by key over our defaults. `None` gives our defaults. | `fr.settings("fransys.toml")` |
| [`paper`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/settings/index.md#the-paper-per-drawing-type) | `None` | A mapping of a `fr.PageKind` to a paper format's name, for that drawing type. | `fr.settings(paper={fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM: "A2"})` |

## `fr.build`

`fr.build(*drafts, ...)` takes the drafts or `Design` objects to merge as `drafts`.

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`releases`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#keeping-designations-fixed-across-revisions) | `None` | A release root. Numbering pins are seeded from the releases stored there, so a released unit keeps its numbers. `None` numbers freely. | `fr.build(d, releases=Path("releases"))` |
| [`settings`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/settings/index.md#frsettings) | `None` | The `fr.Settings` from `fr.settings(...)`, used for this build. `None` uses our defaults. | `fr.build(d, settings=fr.settings(paper={fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM: "A2"}))` |

## `fr.check`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The `BuildResult` to check. Returns its findings plus the KiCad, PDF and render checks, errors first. | `fr.check(result)` |

## `fr.report`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The `BuildResult` to report. Returns one text: a summary line, each ERROR and WARNING with its fix, then counted notes. | `print(fr.report(result))` |

## `fr.write`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The built model whose exports are written. Any ERROR in `fr.check(result)` raises `BuildFailedError` and writes nothing. | `fr.write(result, Path("out"))` |
| [`out_dir`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#export-file-names) | required | The folder that receives the exports: the CSV reports, WAGO XML, overview and one PDF per document. | `fr.write(result, Path("out"))` |
| [`unit`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/units/index.md#writing-one-unit) | `None` | Writes only that unit's own set, with no `overview.html`. `None` writes the whole model. | `fr.write(result, out, unit="pump-board")` |
| [`intermediates`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#export-file-names) | `None` | A folder for SVGs, netlists and `.typ` sources. `None` keeps them in memory. | `intermediates=Path(".fransys")` |
| [`releases`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#export-file-names) | `None` | A release root. With a stored release of the system there, `overview.html` marks what changed since it. `None` marks nothing. | `releases=Path("releases")` |

## `fr.export_names`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The `BuildResult`. Returns the file name `fr.write` gives each export, keyed by kind and subject. Writes nothing. | `fr.export_names(result)` |
| [`unit`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#export-file-names) | `None` | Names only that unit's exports, as `fr.write(unit=)` would. `None` names the whole model's. | `fr.export_names(result, unit="pump-board")` |

## `fr.release`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The built model to release. Any ERROR raises `BuildFailedError` and writes nothing. | `fr.release(result, Path("releases"))` |
| [`into`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#releasing-a-frozen-baseline) | required | The release root. The call writes `<into>/<name>/<version>.<revision>/`. An identical stored listing returns the existing path. | `fr.release(result, Path("releases"))` |
| [`unit`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#releasing-a-frozen-baseline) | `None` | Releases that unit instead of the system. | `fr.release(result, into, unit="pump-board")` |

## `fr.releases`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`root`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#listing-the-releases) | required | The release root to read. Returns each release folder in name, version, revision order. A missing root gives `()`. | `fr.releases(Path("releases"))` |

## `fr.diff`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The built model to compare. Returns the Markdown change list against a stored release. | `fr.diff(result, Path("releases"))` |
| `baselines` | required | The release root that holds the stored release. A missing release raises `FileNotFoundError`. | `fr.diff(result, Path("releases"))` |
| `unit` | `None` | Compares that unit instead of the system. | `fr.diff(result, root, unit="pump-board")` |
| `against` | `None` | A `<version>.<revision>` folder to compare with. `None` takes the release at the model's revision, else the previous one. | `against="1.3"` |

## `fr.verify`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The rebuilt model. Returns one `BASELINE_DIFFERS` ERROR per unit instance, or the system, whose listing drifted, and an INFO (`BASELINE_RULES_MOVED`, `BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED`) for a release cut by an older fransys: `fr.rebaseline` clears it. | `fr.verify(result, Path("releases"))` |
| [`baselines`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/build/index.md#checking-a-baseline-stays-true) | required | The release root with the stored baselines. A unit with no stored baseline is not reported. | `fr.verify(result, Path("releases"))` |

## `fr.rebaseline`

| keyword | default | effect | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `result` | required | The rebuilt model. Re-cuts each stored listing the current rules print differently, in `listing.json` and the manifest only, children before parents. Returns the folders rewritten, `()` when none. A real change raises `BuildFailedError` with `BASELINE_DIFFERS` and writes nothing. | `fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases"))` |
| `baselines` | required | The release root with the stored baselines. | `fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases"))` |
| `unit` | `None` | `None` covers every unit and the system with a stored baseline. A unit covers it and the units below. | `fr.rebaseline(result, root, unit="pump-board")` |

## `fr.parts`

`fr.parts(*packages)` takes part-data package import names. It has no named keyword and returns one `Draft`. Zero names give an empty `Draft`. Example: `fr.parts("demo_parts")`.

## `fr.parts_module`

`fr.parts_module(*sources)` takes the library names to generate a typed parts module for. It has no named keyword and returns the module's text. Example: `fr.parts_module("demo_parts")`.

## `fr.lint`

`fr.lint(*libraries)` takes part-library import names. It has no named keyword and returns their findings, library by library. Zero libraries give `()`. Example: `fr.lint("demo_parts")`.
