<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/settings/index.md -->

# Settings

This page holds the settings of one build: `fr.settings`, the consumer's TOML file, the paper per drawing type, and the `SettingsError` a wrong key raises. Every build uses our defaults until you pass `settings=`.

`SettingsError` and `BuildFailedError` share the base `FransysError`, which is also a bad argument to a facade call. It is a `TypeError` and a `ValueError`, so `except TypeError` and `except ValueError` still catch it.

## `fr.settings`

`fr.settings(path=None, *, paper=None)` returns a `fr.Settings`, a frozen value. With no arguments it gives our defaults. `path` names a TOML file of your own settings. `paper` maps a `fr.PageKind` to a paper's name.

`fr.Settings` has six named fields. `paper` holds the paper formats and the default paper. `paper_by_kind` holds the paper for each drawing type. `font` is empty for our font, else the name and the two font files. `pdf`, `look` and `layout` hold our own values, which a file cannot change. Every other table is read with `Settings.table(name)`.

```python
import fransys as fr

base = fr.settings()
assert base.paper["default"] == "A3"
assert base.paper_by_kind[fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM] == "A2"
```

## The TOML file

A consumer's file names only what differs from our defaults. The merge is key by key. A key the file gives replaces ours. A key it leaves out keeps our value. A file that sets only `default` changes only `default`.

A consumer's project might hold this `fransys.toml`:

```toml
# fransys.toml: only what differs from our defaults
[paper]
default = "A2"
```

The build script reads the file and passes the result to the build. The script below writes the same file into a temporary folder, so it runs as it stands.

```python
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Mapping
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    file.write_text('[paper]\ndefault = "A2"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    s = fr.settings(file, paper={fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM: "A2"})

assert s.paper["default"] == "A2"

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P")
result = fr.build(d, settings=s)
assert result.settings is s
```

A project sets only words, lists and export. The engine numbers (`[layout]`, `[profile]`), the PDF numbers (`[pdf]`), the look (`[look]`) and the stroke widths and dash patterns (`[lines]`, `[dash]`) are ours and fixed. A file that names one of those tables raises `SettingsError`; delete the table.

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    file.write_text("[layout]\nrow_gap = 32\n", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        fr.settings(file)
    except fr.SettingsError as e:
        assert "[layout] is fixed in 0.22; remove it from your settings" in str(e)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected SettingsError")

assert fr.settings().layout["row_gap"] == 24
```

## The font

One build has one font. The grid is the library's fixed 2.5 mm module, so a `[grid]` table raises; delete it.

`[font]` takes the regular and the bold TrueType file, in that order. Each path is relative to the settings file. The widths of the text come from the files themselves. The text sizes are the library's fixed heights: a `[font.heights]` table is refused. The build fails with `SettingsError` when a symbol's fixed text no longer fits its body in the new font, and the PDF is set in the font you name.

```toml
# fransys.toml
[font]
name = "Liberation Sans Narrow"
files = ["fonts/LiberationSansNarrow-Regular.ttf", "fonts/LiberationSansNarrow-Bold.ttf"]
```

Today's schematic engine keeps the built-in font. The keys apply to the drawings of the new engine, and a build with one set gives one `SETTING_NEW_ENGINE_ONLY` WARNING per key; the WARNING goes when the old engine does (MODEL-TEXT).

A `[grid]` table shows the reason.

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    grid = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    grid.write_text("[grid]\nmodule_mm = 2.0\n", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        fr.settings(grid)
    except fr.SettingsError as e:
        assert "the grid is the library's fixed 2.5 mm" in str(e)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected SettingsError")
```

## The paper per drawing type

`paper` maps a drawing type to a paper's name, such as `{fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM: "A2"}`. The formats are closed: `A3` and `A2`, all landscape. A TOML `[paper.formats]` table, a portrait sheet or any other size is refused (`SHEET_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` for an authored sheet). Every PDF that shows that drawing type shows the same layout. Our default puts the block diagram on A2 and every other drawing on A3.

Name the paper per drawing type in Python only. A per-kind key in a TOML file raises.

```python
s = fr.settings(paper={fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM: "A3"})
assert s.paper_by_kind[fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM] == "A3"
assert fr.settings().paper_by_kind[fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM] == "A2"
```

## The words

`[words]` holds the words the drawings and lists print, such as `side_a`, `pin`, `spare`, `no` and `nc`, and the page headings. The PLC list prints the signal words `signal_di`, `signal_do`, `signal_ai_ma`, `signal_ai_v`, `signal_ao_ma`, `signal_ao_v`, `signal_rtd` and `signal_relay_do`. Each word has one key. A key you leave out keeps our word.

```toml
[words]
side_a = "Side A (field)"
```

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    file.write_text('[words]\nside_a = "Side A (field)"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    s = fr.settings(file)

assert s.table("words")["side_a"] == "Side A (field)"
assert s.table("words")["side_b"] == "Side B"
```

## The lists

`[lists.<name>]` holds the columns of one list: `bom`, `plc`, `wires`, `designations`, `cables`, `cores`, `terminal`, `connectors` or `contents`. Each `[[lists.<name>.columns]]` row has the row `field` it prints, the `pdf` word that heads it in the PDF and the `csv` word that heads it in the CSV file. Both words are keys of `[words]`. A list's `pdf_columns` names the fields its PDF prints, when that is fewer than the CSV prints. A consumer's rows replace the list's columns as a whole.

```toml
[[lists.bom.columns]]
field = "mpn"
pdf = "head_mpn"
csv = "csv_mpn"

[[lists.bom.columns]]
field = "count"
pdf = "head_count"
csv = "csv_count"
```

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    columns = '[[lists.bom.columns]]\nfield = "mpn"\npdf = "head_mpn"\ncsv = "csv_mpn"\n'
    file.write_text(columns, encoding="utf-8")
    s = fr.settings(file)

bom = s.table("lists")["bom"]
assert isinstance(bom, Mapping)
assert [row["field"] for row in bom["columns"]] == ["mpn"]
```

## The export files

`[export]` sets which files `fr.write` makes and how it names, places and encodes them. `reports` lists the whole-model reports, in order: `bom`, `plc`, `wires`, `designations`, `cables` and `cores`. The default writes those six. `ring_out` is a seventh kind that is off by default (see below). A name outside those seven raises `SettingsError`. `name_join` joins the prefix, the kind and the fragment of a file name, `version_sign` sits before the version, and `ref_sign` replaces each sign of a designation, so `=A1+C1-K1` gives `A1-C1-K1`.

`data_dir` is the folder of the files that end in one of `data_suffixes`. The CSV files follow `csv_delimiter`, `csv_encoding`, `csv_quoting` (`minimal`, `all`, `nonnumeric` or `none`) and `csv_newline`. Only a `.csv` file takes `csv_encoding`; the others stay UTF-8. `hide_pe` (default `false`, one choice for the whole build) leaves the PE rail's wires and PE symbols on device pins, with their markings, off every drawing sheet. The terminal list and the other lists keep them. `fr.derive.export_form_of(model)` gives the record a build holds.

```toml
[export]
reports = ["bom", "wires"]
csv_delimiter = ";"
csv_encoding = "utf-8-sig"
```

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    file.write_text('[export]\ncsv_delimiter = ";"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    s = fr.settings(file)

assert s.table("export")["csv_delimiter"] == ";"
assert s.table("export")["data_dir"] == "data"
```

## The ring-out sheet

Add `"ring_out"` to `reports` and `fr.write` also writes one `.xlsx` for every PDF of a unit document, named with the PDF's stem (`pump.pdf`, `pump.xlsx`). A SYSTEM, item or location document gets none. The electrician rings out the cabinet line by line on a phone and marks each line. Files in the output folder are replaced on each write, so copy a filled-in sheet out of it before you rebuild.

```toml
[export]
reports = ["bom", "ring_out"]
```

The sheet has a title row (the document's title, number and revision) and a frozen, filterable header. One line follows per wire, then per cable core, then per terminal bridge. A bridge line joins two consecutive bridged terminals. Each group keeps the order of its own list. Twenty empty lines headed `ring_extra` end the sheet for joins the drawing lacks. The columns are `No`, `Type`, `From`, `To`, `Wire / core`, `Colour`, `mm²`, `Drawing`, `Status`, `Found instead` and `Comment`. `Drawing` is the page and frame cell of the From end, empty for a bridge, which is not drawn. `Status` is a dropdown of `OK`, `Wrong` and `Not tested`; empty means not tested. OK shows green and Wrong red. The same model always gives the same bytes.

Every word is a `[words]` key with an English default: `ring_sheet`, `ring_no`, `ring_type`, `ring_wire`, `ring_core`, `ring_from`, `ring_to`, `ring_label`, `ring_colour`, `ring_mm2`, `ring_drawing`, `ring_status`, `ring_ok`, `ring_wrong`, `ring_untested`, `ring_found`, `ring_comment` and `ring_extra`. The Bridge type and the revision word are the existing `bridge` and `revision` keys. Override a value to change a word, for example `ring_status = "State"`.

```python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    file = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    file.write_text('[export]\nreports = ["ring_out"]\n\n[words]\nring_status = "State"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    s = fr.settings(file)

assert s.table("export")["reports"] == ("ring_out",)
assert s.table("words")["ring_status"] == "State"
```

## `SettingsError`

`fr.settings` raises `fr.SettingsError` for a file that is missing, is not TOML, or has a key Fransys does not know. It also raises for a value of another type than ours, for library data in a TOML file, and for a paper name that is not a format. Its message names the file, the key and the keys known there.

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    typo = Path(folder) / "fransys.toml"
    typo.write_text('[paper]\ndefualt = "A2"\n', encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        fr.settings(typo)
    except fr.SettingsError as e:
        assert "known: default, formats" in str(e)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected SettingsError")

    later = Path(folder) / "later.toml"
    later.write_text('[export]\nfrobnicate = 1\n', encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        fr.settings(later)
    except fr.SettingsError as e:
        assert "is not a setting; known:" in str(e)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected SettingsError")
```

## `BuildResult.settings`

`fr.build` returns a `BuildResult`, and its `settings` field holds the `fr.Settings` the build used. Without `settings=` it holds our defaults.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.23/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.23

This page lists what 0.23 adds, what stays refused for now, and the known issues you can meet. No call changes from 0.22.9: no name is added to or removed from the API, and no call needs a new spelling.

## New in 0.23.2

- After a layout ERROR in one drawing set, the drawn-page checks (CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN, OVERLAP and the rest) still run on the other sets; 0.23.1 skipped them all. The ERROR says its set is not drawn. `fr.write` still refuses.

## New in 0.23.1

- A PLC channel's signal name and description print in the PLC list only, never at the pins. The pins draw as in 0.23.0. For `.plc(..., description=)` see `moving-to-0.22.md`, New in 0.23.1.

## New in 0.23.0

- By-others outlines: `unit-outline-by-others` draws a unit that others supply as a dashed outline, and `connector-head` is the symbol for a connector head. Both are `electrical_symbols` symbols.
- `WIDER_THAN_PAGE` and `PAGE_OVERFLOW` name the drawing set, the PDF page, the row and its devices, so you can find the overflow.
- A two-pole switch with a pin turned to the far side draws it as a cross-link; before, a second lane could claim the pin.

## Still refused, for now

- Mated connectors, PCB board documents and harness lines raise an ERROR. A board unit draws as an ordinary unit.
- A terminal with more than two pins raises an ERROR.
- A cable screen connection (`core(SH, ...)`, `spare(SH, at=...)`) raises `SCREEN_DISABLED`; the cable heading still prints "shielded".

## Known issues in 0.23.0

- KI-745: a side tag marker can be left unplaced (`MARKER_UNPLACED`) on a large page of many circuits. A fix is in progress and ships in the release after it lands.
- KI-749: `CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN` or `MARKER_UNPLACED` on a page that also has `PAGE_OVERFLOW`. Fix the overflow first; the others follow it.
- KI-757: a wide marker on a page that does not overflow can leave `CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN`.
- KI-759: a very large two-pole switch fan (24 or more chains per pole) can leave `CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN` and `DANGLING_WIRE_END`.
- KI-762: a hub alone on a page or in a short row can lose a tag pair (`MARKER_UNPLACED`), and a `CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN` can follow. A fix is in progress and ships in the release after it lands.
- KI-746, KI-747: a tag or `WHERE` marker text can overlap a wire or a slot text (`OVERLAP`, looks only).
- KI-748: the `OVERLAP` message does not name both elements yet.

## A supply net behind a fuse prints the fuse

- A supply net behind a fuse or breaker prints its supply name and the tag of the nearest protective device, such as `24V -F2`. The net at the supply keeps `24V`. Two nets that share one name, with no unique protective device between them, raise `RAIL_IDENTITY_SHARED`: put a fuse or breaker between them.

## `DrawnRow.height_g` and `width_g` are now `height` and `width`

- A `Drawing` is in layout units, one eighth of a G, and its rows were always in that unit, so the `_g` suffix was wrong. Rename `row.height_g` to `row.height` and `row.width_g` to `row.width`; the values are the same. An A3 page's `area.w` is 1312.
- A build with a layout ERROR now returns its pages and rows in `result.drawings`, so you can see why; `fr.write` still refuses it.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.22/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.22

This page lists each call that 0.22 adds, changes or removes, with the old spelling and the new one.

## Rating is the elecdef Rating

`fr.derive.Rating` is removed, with `BreakingPoint` and `effective_rating`. A rating is a `fr.elecdef.Rating`: its voltage and current are tuples of `fr.elecdef.Range`, each with the current kind in `at`.
`Rating(voltage_ac_v=Decimal(250))` becomes
`fr.elecdef.Rating(voltage=(fr.elecdef.Range(fr.elecdef.Role.RATED, nom=fr.elecdef.Unit.V(250), at=fr.elecdef.At(fr.elecdef.Current.AC)),))`.
The rating has no breaking fields: a breaking figure is in the function's `[function.block]`
(`breaking_capacity` for a fuse; `icn`, `icu` and `ics` for a breaker). A fuse link with no function states a breaking minimum in its part-level `[block]`.

## Operating has Range and Quantity fields

`fr.derive.Operating` keeps its name. `voltage_ac_v`, `voltage_dc_v`, `nominal_voltage_v`, `min_voltage_v` and `max_voltage_v` are one `voltage` tuple of `Range`
(a nominal with a window is one `Range` with `nom`, `min` and `max`). `max_current_ac_a` and `max_current_dc_a` are `max_current`;
`fault_current_ac_a` and `fault_current_dc_a` are `fault_current`. The rest drop the unit suffix and hold a `fr.elecdef.Quantity`,
for example `fault_time_constant=fr.elecdef.Unit.MS(15)`. In a part file the keys are the same names; see `parts.md`.

## Current comes from elecdef

The AC/DC enum is `fr.elecdef.Current` (`Current.AC`, `Current.DC`). The old model enum is gone; the authoring string `current="ac"` is unchanged.

## A rail is declared

Bridged DC or PE strips are no longer rails: add `rail=True` to the bridged `run` or `d.terminal_strip` that is the rail. An unflagged terminal draws as a terminal, and `d.detail.rail_bond` is gone with the `rail` link kind.

## Removed in 0.22

Each row is a name that 0.22 removed. A removed attribute raises an error that names its row here.

| 0.21 spelling | 0.22 spelling |
|---|---|
| `fr.ABOVE`, `fr.BELOW`, `d.layout.side(target, fr.ABOVE)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1486) |
| `fr.IT`, `fr.EARTHED` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1494); supplies are the earthed default only |
| `fr.BuildErrors` | `fr.BuildFailedError`, e.g. `except fr.BuildFailedError:` |
| `fr.MergeConflict` | `fr.MergeConflictError`, e.g. `except fr.MergeConflictError:` |
| `d.busbar(a, b)` | `d.detail.busbar(a, b)` |
| `d.rating(part, function)`, `d.operating(part, function)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); read part data through the part's elecdef `Rating` |
| `d.detail.wire(a, b, wire=w, label=, n=)` | `d.series(a, b, wire=w)`; `label=` and `n=` have no replacement |
| `d.detail.star(src, targets, wire=w)` | `d.series(src, t, wire=w)` for each target |
| `d.detail.net(name, *pins, kind=)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); connect with `d.series(a, b)` |
| `d.detail.rail_bond(a, b)`, link kind `rail` | Declare the rail with `rail=True`; bond PE with `d.series(incoming_pe, pe, wire=(GNYE, 1.5))` |
| `d.layout.chain(*functions, beside=...)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); `d.series` names the path |
| `d.layout.page_title(thing, text)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); the default page title stays |
| `d.layout.symbol(target, symbol, port_map)` | `symbol = "..."` on the part file's `[[function]]` entry |
| `d.layout.break_before(group)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); order with `d.layout.order(*groups)` |
| `d.layout.keep_together(*groups)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490) |
| `d.layout.draw_in(function, group)` | Removed; `d.series` and `group=` place the function |
| `d.layout.pins_below(box)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490); `hide_unused_pins=True` stays |
| `d.layout.profile(sheet=, column_gap=, row_gap=, row_spacing=, route_margin=, text_height_mm=, min_text_height_mm=, marker_padding=, route_turn_penalty=, route_crossing_penalty=, actuator_each_contact=, band_ranks=, group_ranks=)`, `d.layout.sheet(name, ...)` | `d.layout.profile(hide_unused_pins=False)` is the only keyword left; order groups with `d.layout.order(*groups)`; paper with `fr.settings(paper=...)` |
| `@fr.unit(..., wiring={...})` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1493); per-wire colour: `d.series(a, b, wire=(BU, 0.75))` |
| `fr.unit(..., class_code="K")`, `d.add(defn, None)` | `d.add(board, "U1")`: an authored tag, a bare string; `None` is no longer allowed |
| `[font.heights]` in the settings file | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1458); delete the table |
| `text_height_mm`, `min_text_height_mm`, `TEXT_TOO_SMALL` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1458); text heights are fixed library data |
| `fr.document(..., add=, remove=)`, presets `HARNESS_DRAWING`, `PCB_SCHEMATIC` | `fr.document(preset, subject, cover=, logo=, notice=)`; the preset sets the pages. `remove=(fr.PageKind.SHEET_INDEX,)` and every other `remove=` has no replacement: a preset prints its fixed pages |
| `d.add(defn, tag, unused=(...))` | `d.device(tag, part, unused=True)` for the unit's own open pins; `d.unused(pc.x3[3], pc.x4_1)` in the carrier for a unit's boundary points it leaves open (0.22.3) |
| `Port.role` (`PortRole`) | `Port.boundary` (`fr.derive.PortBoundary`), and new `Port.pin_role` |
| `Cable.core(which, a, fn)` with a PE-bar function | Use a PE terminal strip: `W1.core(GNYE, x1[1].outer)` |
| `DrawnReading.units` | No change: the name never existed at either version; the unit is `DrawnPageReading.unit` per page |
| `Fn.limits(rating=, operating=)`, `Terminal.limits(...)` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1490) |
| Mated connector, PCB board document, harness line | Refused with ERROR `MATES_DISABLED` (R1216); draw the connection as a cable or wires |
| Terminal part with more than two pins | Refused with ERROR `TERMINAL_MORE_THAN_TWO_PINS`; use a two-pin part: `d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 2)` |
| `[colours]`, `[grid]`, `[layout]`, `[profile]`, `[pdf]`, `[look]`, `[lines]`, `[dash]`, `[reference]`, `[frame]`, `[stub]`, `[wire_label]`, `[harness]`, `[title_block]`, `[revision_table]`, `[revision]`, `[designation]` | Removed on purpose: Fransys decides (R1458); a `SettingsError` names the table; delete it |
| Part schema 1 (`schema = 1`) | `schema = 2`; convert with `python -m fransys migrate-parts DIR` |
| `TERMINAL_POINT_OVERFILLED` (new in 0.22, no 0.21 spelling) | Set `conductors_per_clamp = 2` in the terminal part's `[connection]` table, or use a twin part, or bridge a second terminal |

## New in 0.23.1

- `.plc(..., description="...")` gives a PLC channel a line of text. The PLC list prints it in a `description` column beside the signal name (PDF and `plc.csv`, which gains the column). The description lives in the PLC list only, and the Wago rack XML is unchanged. A blank description raises. listing_version 9: no listing text moves; a stored model of schema 25 is refused: rebuild it.

## New in 0.22.9

- The Wago rack XML `<Modules>` follows the CDP reference, so every consumer's file changes. A module is named `<order>_<channels><kind>_<letter>` with the kind DI, AI, DO or AO (an RTD is AI, a relay output DO, an analogue output AO). A module whose channels mix kinds is named by the bare order number. A channel is named by its bare signal name, else `<kind><Nr>` (DO0, DI14). An analogue channel has no `Nr`. A mixed module lists outputs first and restarts `Nr` for each direction (decision wago-0003).
- New spellings: `.plc(signal, name, routing=)`, `.plc(name=)` and `.plc(configured=False)` on a module's channel handle, `.scale(raw=, eng=)` with no unit, and `.scale(...)` on a spare analogue channel. `SCALING_UNIT_EMPTY` is gone: a blank unit raises at the call. `PLC_SIGNAL_NAME_TWICE` is new.
- Page text: pages replace sheets. The title block shows "page m of N" and has no sheet cell. A reference prints the page number alone (`p<n>:<cell>`), led by the far PDF's scope path across PDFs. The PDF order is the cover, the drawings, then the index and the lists. Drawings can move: the wider reserved reference text re-lays out some pages.
- listing_version 8: no listing text moves. A stored model of schema 24 is refused: rebuild it. A wire made inside a `d.function` block now carries that block. A pin wired only in one other block that draws a function of its own is drawn there. A terminal, supply, connector or PLC channel stays with its item (decision model-0442).
- Tags stand at a symbol corner, top-left first, then bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right, one grid step out, then turned. Tags move on many pages; nothing to change in your code.
- A unit's drawing no longer changes with the names of the units above it.
- `OVERLAP` now also counts text resting on a wire's edge and diagonal runs. A new `OVERLAP` WARNING is a Fransys looks defect: report it.
- Fixed: phantom loops around a part's internal links with no conductor (KI-732), and a trunk drawn through a neighbouring card (KI-731).
- Fixed: a connection lost when a net crossed a page cut twice, as with two output cards (KI-739), and a reference leg starting inside its trunk (KI-736).

### Known issues in 0.22.9

- `MARKER_UNPLACED` on a 40-circuit demo-flags build leaves one tag marker unplaced at two salts. It is old (KI-745) and fixed in 0.23.1.

## New in 0.22.8

- One `terminals.csv` holds every terminal strip, and one `connectors.csv` every board. They replace the files per strip or board: read the one file instead (decision model-0437).
- `[export] hide_pe = true` leaves the PE rail's wires and the PE symbols on device pins, with their markings, off every drawing sheet; the lists keep them. A flagged PE terminal never draws. Off by default: drawings do not change (decisions model-0435, el-0119).

## New in 0.22.7

- A leg's run is cleared of a footprint's pin tips. Only the PE terminal joined by `d.earth` stops being a spare. The shorts this drew there (`DRAWING_SHORTS_NETS`) are gone (KI-708, layout-0446, model-0429). No action.
- A copied cut piece joins no pins: its ends pair two by two (KI-710). No action.
- `OVERLAP`, `WIRE_OVER_MARKER` and the width refusal name the elements and the fix. The guide gained the width table, net rows, bare-pin use and the full-cabinet path. No action.

## New in 0.22.6

- A revision cut by 0.22.4 or earlier reads again, with no rebaseline needed. `fr.verify` finds nothing to report. `fr.release` cuts the next revision, also for a container that pins such a revision (decisions model-0289, model-0428).

## New in 0.22.5

- listing_version 7: a list end prints the pin's marking when it is set and unique under its printed prefix, else its name (decisions model-0428, model-0431).
- 0.22.5 cannot read a revision cut by 0.22.4 or earlier: `fr.verify` reports `BASELINE_TOO_OLD`, and `fr.release` and `fr.rebaseline` refuse. Stay on 0.22.4 to release; 0.22.6 reads them again.
- A connected cable screen (`core(SH, ...)`, `spare(SH, at=...)`) is refused with `SCREEN_DISABLED` until screen connections return; the cable heading still prints "shielded" (decision model-0430).

## New in 0.22.1

- `python -m fransys migrate-parts DIR` rewrites a schema 1 parts library to the 0.22 format (decision 0474). `DIR` is the library's folder (the one holding `library.toml` and `parts/`) or a folder above it, never `parts/`.
- A removed 0.22 name raises an error that names the new spelling and the row above, from one table that is deleted at the 0.23 tag (decision 0475).

## New in 0.22.3

- `d.unused(pc.x3[3], pc.x4_1)` declares a nested unit's boundary points, or a port, that the design leaves open on purpose (decision 0481). The unit's own `unused=` stays the unit's fact. It reverses the `add(unused=)` part of the 0.22 removal.
- Two ERROR codes check it: `UNUSED_NOT_BOUNDARY` and `UNUSED_POINT_WIRED`; a point listed twice raises an `AuthorError`.

## New in 0.22.2

- The per-channel engineering range returns as `.plc(...).scale(unit, raw=, eng=)`, written to the Wago rack XML exactly as in 0.21.2 (decision model-0425).
- Three ERROR codes check it: `SCALING_RANGE_INVALID`, `SCALING_NOT_ANALOGUE` and `SCALING_UNIT_EMPTY`.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.20/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.20

This page lists each call that 0.20 adds or changes, with the old spelling and the new one.

## A baseline cut by an older fransys

`fr.verify` compares a stored listing under the rules of the `fransys` that cut it. When a later
release printed a rule differently, it gives `BASELINE_RULES_MOVED_NOTE` (INFO) for that release, and
`fr.release` refuses over it. `fr.rebaseline` is the new call that clears it: it re-cuts the stored
`listing.json` and the manifest under today's rules and leaves every export as it was.

Run `fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases"))` once and commit the rewritten files. The worked example
is in `build.md`, after "Checking a baseline stays true".

## A finding carries its fix

`fr.Finding` has a new field `fix`: the text that clears it, `<valid values>. Write: <corrected call>`. `fr.report` prints the finding's own `fix`, and `BuildFailedError.findings` holds the same rows, so a test reads `exc.findings[0].fix`. `LABEL_UNPLACED` is now INFO (a Fransys defect, send the smallest model). A `fr.Finding(...)` you build yourself with severity ERROR or WARNING must pass `fix=`.

## Renames in the change list

A listing now carries item keys (version 2), so the change list follows a rename: "Renamed -A1 → -A2"
replaces a removal and an addition, and `changes.csv` writes `renamed` in the `change`
column. A release cut before 0.20 has no keys; 0.22 refuses it (`BASELINE_TOO_OLD`); `fr.rebaseline` cannot re-cut it, so `fr.release` a new revision and the old one stays as released.

## A derive row type renamed

`fr.derive.BridgePiece`, the row that holds one jumper-bridge image, is now `fr.derive.BridgePieceRow`,
so it no longer shares a name with the symbol's `electrical_symbols.BridgePiece` (`"line"` or `"tick"`).
No alias keeps the old name. Only code that names the type changes; the fields are as they were.

`DocumentScope.bom_top_level` is now `DocumentScope.top_level`.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.19/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.19

This page lists each call that 0.19 moves or changes, with the old spelling and the new one.
A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below.

## The detail calls

Four calls moved to `d.detail`, with their keywords unchanged. The old names raise an `AuthorError`
that names the new home. There is no alias: one task has one spelling.

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `d.wire(a, b, wire=...)` | `d.series(a, b, wire=...)` | A path is `d.series`. A hand-wired hop is for a case no series writes (detail.md). |
| `d.busbar(a, b)` | `d.detail.busbar(a, b)` | A busbar joins two fixed pins, a detail case. |

A unit body's design moves the same way: `u.wire(...)` becomes `u.series(...)`. `d.earth`,
`d.mate` and `W1.core` keep their spellings.

## Grouped contacts

| before | after |
|---|---|
| one series per contact: `d.series(a.A_L1, k1.co_1.no, ...)`, and again for `co_2` and `co_3` | `q = d.poles(k1.co_1, k1.co_2, k1.co_3)`, then one `d.series(a, q.no, m1, ...)` |
| three single-pole changeover symbols | one three-pole symbol; with `selector=True` its throws face the line |

## From d.wire to d.series

Most `d.wire` calls were a current path written hop by hop. Write the path as one series instead:
it pairs the poles and takes the next free terminal or core.

A control path from rail to rail:

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
k1 = d.device("K1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, s1.no["13"], ...), d.wire(s1.no["14"], k1.coil["A1"], ...), ...
d.series(dc.plus, s1.no, k1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

A power path through a strip and a cable to a motor:

```python
from fransys.colours import BK

x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)))
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")

# before: one d.wire per pole to X1, one W1.core per core, one d.wire per motor pin
d.series(ac, k1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
```

A fixed terminal, as an as-built cabinet numbers them. `x1[3]` takes the place of the next free
terminal. `x1[1:4]` is terminals 1, 2 and 3 as one three-pole element, the end excluded. A tuple puts
one terminal on each pole when they sit on different strips. A fixed terminal counts as taken, so a
strip passed whole later skips it. A tuple that runs in order on one strip raises and names the
slice to write:

```python
x2 = d.terminal_strip("X2", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
h1 = d.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
x3 = d.terminal_strip("X3", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 6)

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, x2[3]), d.wire(x2[3].outer, h1.lamp["1"]), ...
d.series(dc.plus, x2[3], h1.lamp, x2[4], dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
# three phases on terminals 1, 2 and 3, and one terminal per pole across strips
d.series(ac, k1.main, x3[1:4], wire=(BK, 2.5))
x4, x5 = d.terminal_strip("X4", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4), d.terminal_strip("X5", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4)
d.series(d.device("Q9", "DEMO-MCB-3P").element, (x2[5], x4[3], x5[3]), wire=(BK, 2.5))
```

## Behaviour that changed

| before | now | why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.derive.takes_energy` is `True` for a `load` only | `True` for a `load`, an `actuator` and a `coil` | A motor or coil draws from its supply, so `load_limits` counts its `nominal_current_a`. A part may still state `energy`. |
| A series through a cable landed the GNYE core only when the strip before it had a `pe=` part, else it raised. | The core lands on the load's PE port. The near end is the strip's PE terminal, else earthed open. | A cable's protective core reaches its load without a hand wire (author-0044). |
| A wire to the load's PE port after such a series built a `GNYE_NOT_PE` ERROR. | It raises an `AuthorError` that names the series. | The core is already landed; a second landing is refused at the call (author-0044). |
| `d.series(j1.x1, w5, j2.x1, ...)` between two connectors raised `has no poles: name its pins`; each pin pair was a `d.wire` call. | The series pairs the two connectors' pins in pin order. A function with no line side in the middle, or at one end against a supply, a rail or a function with poles, still raises. Unequal pin counts raise and name both counts. | One derive fact orders a sideless end's pins (model-0242). |
## Channels a series takes

A series now takes a PLC channel itself. Pass the module whole and it takes the lowest free channel
(authoring.md, how channels are numbered). A script that fixes every channel, `a1.di_7`, still works.

A package that keeps the channel map of existing software checks it once. Build the package both
ways, with the channels fixed and with the module passed whole, and compare the PLC list. If the
two lists are equal, use the core form. Where they differ, keep the fixed form for those channels.

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


def plc_list(fixed: bool) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """The PLC list of a two-sensor package, the channels fixed or taken by the series."""
    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    a1 = d.device("A1", "DEMO-PLC-DI-4P")
    for number in (1, 2):
        sensor = d.device(f"S{number}", "DEMO-PB-NC")
        sensor.sw.plc(fr.DI, f"Sensor {number}")
        target = getattr(a1, f"di_{number}") if fixed else a1
        d.series(dc.plus, sensor.sw, target, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return [(r.pin, r.signal_name) for r in fr.derive.plc_channel_rows(fr.build(d).model)]


assert plc_list(fixed=True) == plc_list(fixed=False)  # equal: use the core form
```

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.16-and-0.17/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.16 and 0.17

This page covers a move from 0.15 to 0.16, to 0.17, or across both. If you are on 0.16, read the 0.17 section only.
Nothing in `fr.__all__` is removed or renamed. A stored model written by 0.15 or 0.16 no longer loads.

## Moving from 0.16 to 0.17

Each change below has the old spelling, the new one and the fix.

| where | 0.16 | 0.17 | what to change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stored models | Schema 17. | Schema 18: facing is stored on every link marker. An older model raises `SchemaVersionError`. | Rebuild with `fr.build`. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. |
| `PlcChannelRow` (PLC-PIN-ROWS, model-0209) | One row per channel, with `channel_designation`. | One row per pin, with `port`, `pin` and `channel_name`, and no `channel_designation`. `wired_to` holds the far ends of that pin alone. | Read `pin` and `channel_name` where you read `channel_designation`. |
| `PLC_COLUMNS` and `plc_list_rows` | Built on `channel_designation`. | `pin`, `channel_name`, `signal`, `signal_name`, `wired_to`. | Update code that picks a column by name or position. |
| `UNIT_CONNECTOR_DANGLING` (DANGLING-RETIRE, model-0219) | A `WARNING` for a spare terminal or port of a unit. | Retired: the code no longer exists. | A filter that names it now matches nothing; remove it. |
| `PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH` message | Names each channel by its module. | Names each channel by its pins, such as `-A1:1`. | Code that matches the old text must match the pin form. |

Other 0.17 changes need no code change:

- The PLC list prints one row per pin, spare pins included.
- A PLC request binds the channel it is wired to even when that channel's net holds other devices. A request of the wrong kind yields the channel to one of the right kind (model-0211).
- Several requests wired to one channel give `PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH`. Request that channel once, on one of the devices. 0.18 gives one clear finding.
- A finding message names an untagged unit by its name and revision, as its title block prints it. `unit unit` no longer appears (overview-0003).
- A coil switched by a channel pin stands under that channel (layout-0208).
- A beside branch under a host pin no longer fails. That was a 0.16.0 regression (layout-0174).
- A terminal whose part has a protective link, such as a fuse terminal, is no longer a rail terminal (model-0215).
- PDF navigation: link markers and sheet-index rows link, viewer page labels show the sheet text, and the outline lists sheets and devices (pdf-0029, pdf-0034).
- A new package, `fransys-el`, comes in with `fransys`. A lock file gains one package (layout-0192).
- Cable page texts come out in reading order (render-0011).

## Moving from 0.15 to 0.16

### What may newly stop your build

| change | what you see | the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Stored models use schema 17 (0.15: 15) | `SchemaVersionError`: "this build reads schema version 17" | Rebuild the model with `fr.build`. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. |
| `PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS` is a new `ERROR` | A PLC request whose wiring ties several channels of its signal kind, none on a direct conductor, used to take the first one silently. Now it binds none. | Wire the request to one channel. The message names the request and every tied channel (model-0211). |
| `PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH` message | It now names the asked kind, the channel, the channel's kind and both fixes. The severity is unchanged. | Ask for the channel's kind, or rewire to a channel of the asked kind. |
| `CABLE_PAIR_INVALID` is a new part-file `ERROR` | A `[cable_product] pairs` entry names a core out of range, a core in two pairs, a screen that is not `SH`, or an `SH` core as a pair core. | Correct the pair list in the part file. |
| `CABLE_CORE_COUNT` counts open cores | A cable with `spare` or one-ended screen cores now counts them toward its part's core count, so a warning can clear or appear. | The message names the remedy. |
| `HintError` for a group with no column | It names the group that took the devices, the loop and the `d.layout.chain` fix. It is still an error. | Apply the `d.layout.chain(...)` it prints (layout-0195). |
| `TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW` names `d.layout.page_title` | The `=F1 =F2` group-label fallback is gone. A title that fits no form is cut with "…". It stays a `WARNING`. | Give the page a short title with `d.layout.page_title`. |

These findings no longer fire, so a script that expects them changes:

- `DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS` is an `ERROR` for a `SCHEMATIC` page only when the document has no other content page. A list with rows, a `HARNESS_DRAWING` with a cable or a `BLOCK_DIAGRAM` with a sheet is enough (pdf-0033). Harness and diagram errors are unchanged.
- `UNUSED_CONTRADICTED` is checked at the unit that declares `unused=`. Declaring a passed-up interface unused on the outer unit no longer warns (model-0210).
- `LONE_CELL` skips an item box over a unit's open boundary functions (layout-0202).

### Output changes

Drawings and PDFs change byte for byte. Re-check any golden you keep.

- **Page pad.** Schematic ink keeps two wiring lanes (`PAGE_PAD`) inside the frame line, so every page moves (layout-0187).
- **Idle pins and terminals.** A connector pin or terminal that no wire inside the unit reaches is not drawn on the unit's own pages. The parent's black box keeps it, and its table still lists it (layout-0197, layout-0202). A unit with nothing left to draw adds no schematic page.
- **Connector tables.** `CONNECTOR_LIST` prints one table per connector with Pin, Net, Mate and Ends. Style, pin count and gender leave the PDF table. `connectors.csv` keeps them and gains an `ends` column (pdf-0030).
- **Boundary boxes.** A boundary box prints its landed pins, not the interface field name (model-0206).
- **Cable names.** A cable end that is a connector names it (`+C1-A1-X1`) on the cable page and in the cable list.
- **Spare cores and pairs.** `Cable.spare(...)` and a one-ended screen from `Cable.core` draw as open rows with a blank stub. A part file's `pairs` draw pair brackets. The cable list shows pairs (model-0213, layout-0207).
- **Beside chains.** `d.layout.chain(beside=...)` joins its host by one or two end nets, a one-pin box or a box head, with no marker. A box-pin run stands a grid off the pin.
- **Titles.** The title block prints the first form of `derive.page_title_forms` that fits. A strip terminal reads as its strip once ("-X1") (pdf-0028, pdf-0032).
- **Sheets page.** `PageKind.SHEET_INDEX` is in every preset, after the notes. It lists Sheet, Title and Page. Block diagram sheets read `B1`, `B2` (pdf-0031). `remove=(fr.PageKind.SHEET_INDEX,)` drops it.
- **cores.csv.** It lists every cable core with both ends, its pair and its spare mark (CORES-CSV).
- **PLC list.** Signals print in datasheet words (`DI`, `AI (mA)`, `DO (relay)`). A channel with no device and no wire prints `spare`. The CSV keeps the enum values.
- **A bridged run outside a block** takes no terminals, so its terminals join the block of their first circuit wire (author-0037).

### API names

`fr.__all__` gains no name and loses none. `fr.__version__` is new, read from `importlib.metadata`. It is not in `__all__`, so `from fransys import *` skips it.

| where | new |
|---|---|
| authoring | `d.layout.page_title(thing, text)`; `Cable.spare(*cores, at=...)`; `Cable.core` for an `SH` core earthed at one end |
| part file | `[cable_product] pairs`, and the demo part `DEMO-CBL-2X2X0.75-SP` |
| `fr.PageKind` | `SHEET_INDEX` |
| `fr.derive` rows | `OpenCoreRow`, `SheetIndexRow`, `open_core_rows`, `sheet_index_rows`, `plc_list_rows`, `connector_rows_of`, `CONNECTOR_LABELS` |
| `fr.derive` facts | `function_is_reached`, `port_is_reached`, `connector_items`, `unit_connector_items`, `signal_word`, `cores_text` |
| `fr.derive` titles | `page_title`, `page_title_forms`, `short_title`, `sheets`, `diagram_sheets`, `sheet_text`, `set_page_text`, `sheet_counter_text`, `sheet_title_text` |
| records | `layout.page_title`, `layout.open_core_wire`, `facet.open_core`, and `CableProductFacet.pairs` with `CorePair` |

`d.layout.chain(beside=)` now accepts one end net on the host and a one-pin box at the chain's end.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.15/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.15

This page lists each call, name and finding that 0.15 changes, with the old spelling and the new one.
A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below. The version is read with `importlib.metadata.version("fransys")`; there is no `fr.__version__`.

## Renamed and changed names

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `text_height` in `layout.profile(...)`, an int in `G`, default 8 | `text_height_mm`, a Decimal in mm, default 1.8 | The text size is a capital height in mm (ISO 3098), not a count of grid units. Since 0.22 it is not a profile keyword and not a setting: the heights are the library's. |
| `min_text_mm` in `layout.profile(...)` | `min_text_height_mm`, default 1.8 | It is the floor for `text_height_mm`, in the same unit. Since 0.22 it is gone: the heights are the library's and no floor is checked. |
| `text_mm` and `min_text_mm` on a readability page row | `text_height_mm` and `min_text_height_mm` | The same two quantities under the new names. A unit row takes the smallest `text_height_mm`. |
| `module_mm` scales symbols, gaps and text | `module_mm` sets the grid pitch only | Text and line widths are fixed in mm. Set the text size with `text_height_mm`. |

## New keyword

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.write(result, out_dir)` | `fr.write(result, out_dir, releases=into)` | `releases` is the folder you pass to `fr.release`. It defaults to `None`, which marks nothing. |

## The system overview

`fr.write` writes `overview.html` beside the PDFs. The page is one file and needs no network. Its switches are Colour by, Find, Parts, Select and Theme, and View inside a unit.

- **Changes** is new. It appears only when `releases` holds a release of the system, the one at the model's revision or else the previous one.
- Without `releases`, or with no release there, the page has no Changes switch.
- The Changes switch applies only to a whole-system write; a unit write gets no Changes page.

## Drawing and readability

- `d.ac_supply` no longer draws power symbols at its pins; it keeps AC rails as terminals and references.
- The readability rows have a new column, `single_contact_images_other_page`, counting the single-contact images whose one contact is on another page.

## Checks and findings

- `check` now places `overview.html` and returns its findings, so a whole-system or unit `write` meets them at the same gate. `build` does not.
- `OVERVIEW_UNPLACED` is new. It is an `ERROR`, raised when the overview placer finds no room for a view.
- The `DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP`, `DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX`, `DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX` and `DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP` findings also check the views of the overview.

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.14/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.14

This page lists every `fr.derive` name 0.14 removes, and what to use instead.
`fr.derive` now holds the names a consumer needs to read a model, and every one has a guide entry. The rest stay in the workspace for layout, render and the outputs. A consumer script that used a removed name changes as below.

## Removed names

| removed | use instead | why |
|---|---|---|
| `location_node_designation` | `node_designation` | It prints any aspect node's signed path, `+` or `=`, so the name no longer says location. |
| `number`, `allocate_plc` | `fr.build(d)` | They are passes; the facade runs them. |
| `ext_usage`, `ExtUsage` | none | A migration diagnostic with no consumer use. |
| `overview_graph`, `OverviewGraph`, `OverviewLink`, `OverviewLinkKind`, `OverviewNode`, `OverviewPort`, `OverviewSignal` | none; use `fr.derive.items`, `ports` and `conductors` | The overview output is being reshaped; its graph types are not stable. |
| `box_pairs`, `BoxPair`, `draws_as_line`, `supply_share`, `connector_box_lines`, `connector_at_line_end`, `line_conductors`, `line_stub_line`, `check_side_hints` | the model records: `fr.derive.conductors`, `harness_line_ends`, `line_designation` | Drawing helpers. The model records hold the facts they read. |
| `black_box_unit`, `drawing_set_is_replica_only`, `is_black_box_item`, `schematic_functions`, `own_nodes`, `enclosing_boards`, `first_leg`, `rail_pairs`, `link_state`, `LinkState`, `changeover_throws`, `Throws`, `owned_contacts`, `Indexes`, `build_indexes` | none, or `fr.derive.functions` and `aspect_nodes` | Layout internals. |
| `profile_of` | read the `layout.profile` table of the model | The profile is a record. |
| `physical_nets`, `unused_terminals` | `fr.derive.net_of`, `fr.derive.port_is_unused` | One net, one port at a time. |
| `terminal_strips` | `fr.derive.terminal_items`, `fr.derive.unit_strips` | The kept pair covers a model and a unit. |
| `unit_items`, `unit_subtree` | filter `fr.derive.items` by `item.unit` | A plain filter of a kept table. |
| `current_revision`, `same_version` | `fr.derive.revision_history`, `fr.derive.release_order` | Compare the ordered pairs. |
| `document_unit` | `document.unit` | A field of the document record. |
| `list_context` | pass the location node you want to a row function's `context` | A value the caller passes. |
| `connector_label`, `connector_segments`, `designation_holder`, `takes_parents_designation`, `is_own_unit_root`, `is_sole_unit_root`, `standalone` | `fr.derive.item_designation`, `printed_designation` | The designation functions print the text; the helpers behind them are internal. |
| `core_colour`, `conductors_on_item` | `fr.derive.cable_rows`, `fr.derive.conductors` | The rows carry the colour; the conductors table carries the rest. |
| `cell_parts`, `cell_text`, `column_rows`, `column_values`, `pin_lines` | read the fields of a row and order them by the `*_COLUMNS` constant | Output formatting. |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md -->

# Finding codes

Every code Fransys can emit, with severity, stage, who acts, meaning and fix, on five pages by source.

A finding's message names each thing as the drawings print it. An item reads as its designation, a port as its port designation, a wire as its ends and a tagged unit as the word unit and its tag, `unit -U1`. A unit with no tag reads as its name and revision alone, as its title block prints them. A thing with no printed text reads as its kind alone. A message never prints a `name=` key or an Id. A renamed key changes no message (decision overview-0003).

"Who acts" is one of four. `consumer`: change your design as the fix says. `part author`: the part library's author fixes the part file as the fix says. `Fransys`: a defect in layout or an output, so send the smallest model that shows it. `note`: nothing is wrong.

Every `Finding` row carries its own `fix`: `<valid values>. Write: <corrected call>`, filled with that finding's names and values. A test reads `exc.findings` (from `BuildFailedError`) or `fr.check(result)` and finds the template: `<subject>` and `<other>` stand for the finding's first and second subject. `fr.report` and the `BuildFailedError` message print them filled with those subjects' names. A code no call clears starts with `No call clears this:`. The worked example is in `build.md`, under "write".

- [`findings-validators.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-validators/index.md): the model checks.
- [`findings-build.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-build/index.md): the build, `release` and the library load.
- [`findings-release.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-release/index.md): the build, `release`, `verify` and the baseline check.
- [`findings-render.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-render/index.md): layout and the drawing stage.
- [`findings-pdf.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-pdf/index.md): the PDF output.
- [`findings-kicad.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-kicad/index.md): the KiCad import.
- [`findings-parts.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-parts/index.md): the part-file lint.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-validators/index.md -->

# Finding codes: validators

Codes the model checks emit. The build, release and library load codes are in [`findings-build.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-build/index.md). Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ASPECT_CROSS_PARENT | ERROR | validators | consumer | An aspect node's parent belongs to a different aspect (function, location or product). | Give each location a parent of its own aspect, a location. Write: d.location("BATT", "Battery bay", within="HOLD") |
| ASPECT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | An aspect node's parent chain loops back on itself. | Make the parents of locations form a tree, never a loop. Write: d.location("BATT", "Battery bay", within="HOLD") |
| BOUNDARY_NOT_IN_UNIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's boundary function belongs to an item outside that unit's subtree. | Declare as the unit's boundary only a function of an item built inside that unit. Write: d.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", interface=True) |
| BOUNDARY_UNCONNECTED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's boundary function is not connected across the unit nor declared unused. | Wire each boundary function across the unit, or declare it unused on purpose: inside the unit for its own fact, d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P", interface=True, unused=True); in the design that adds it for a point it leaves to another carrier. Write: d.unused(pc.x3[3], pc.x4_1) |
| CABLE_CORES_FEWER | WARNING | validators | consumer | A cable item carries fewer cores than its product has core colours. | Use as many cores as the product has colours, each wired or marked spare. Write: W1.spare() |
| CABLE_CORES_MORE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable item carries more cores than its product has core colours. | Use as many cores as the product has colours, each wired or marked spare. Write: W1.spare() |
| CONDUCTOR_ON_UNINSTALLED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A conductor lands on an item that is not marked installed. | Mark the item installed, or remove the conductor that lands on it. Write: d.device("Q9", "DEMO-MCB-3P") |
| CONNECTOR_WIRED_WITHOUT_MATE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A conductor from outside a nested unit lands directly on its boundary connector, whose part gender is male or female (genderless or unstated passes). | End a cable's cores at the connector's pins. Write: d.cable("W1", P.CBL).core(1, plug[1], connector[1]) |
| CONTAINMENT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | An item's physical-containment parent chain loops back on itself. | Make physical containment a tree: no item sits inside itself. Write: d.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", parent=k1) |
| CORE_INDEX_PAST_PRODUCT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable core is numbered past the core count of the cable's product. | Number the cores from 1 to the product's core count. Write: W1.core(3, x1[1], x1[2]) |
| CORE_ON_PE_NOT_GNYE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable core that is not green-yellow (GNYE) lands on a port with role PE; a screen core (`SH`) is exempt. | The PE core is GNYE (IEC 60204-1): land the GNYE core on the PE port, and another core elsewhere. Write: W1.core(GNYE, a, b) |
| DOCUMENT_UNIT_UNRESOLVED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A document's `unit_name` matches no unit, or more than one. | Document each placement with what `d.add` returned; the unit's own PDF comes from its release write. Write: fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, placed, cover=Path("cover.md")) |
| FUNCTION_HALF_CONNECTED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A two-port coil, load, contact, switch, protection or actuator is connected at one port and open at the other. | Wire both ports of the function. Write: d.series(a, b) |
| GNYE_NOT_PE_DECLARED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A green-yellow conductor is on a net that a declared net lists and that is not PE (IEC 60445 keeps green-yellow for PE). | Use green-yellow only on the PE net, which `d.earth` declares. Write: d.earth(*pins) |
| GNYE_NOT_PE_UNDECLARED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A green-yellow conductor is on a net that is not PE and that no declared net lists (IEC 60445 keeps green-yellow for PE). | Use green-yellow only on the PE net, which `d.earth` declares. Write: d.earth(*pins) |
| HARNESS_HOLDS_PLC_MODULE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC module sits under an item made with `d.harness`. | Put the PLC modules under a rack, not a harness, so they print flat. Write: d.rack("U1", name="plc") |
| HARNESS_WITHOUT_TAG | ERROR | validators | consumer | A harness (marked, or with a cable child) has no tag or assigned designation, so it has no label. | Give the harness a tag so it has a label. Write: d.harness("W5") |
| ITEM_PART_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | An item's functions or ports do not match its part's templates (missing, extra, duplicated, or differing in name, kind, role or marking). | Make the item's functions and ports match its part's templates, by building it from the part as it stands. Write: d.device("Q1", "DEMO-MCB-3P") |
| ITEM_WITHOUT_PART | INFO | validators | note | A non-external item has no `part`, so its functions are authored directly, not checked against templates. | Usually nothing to fix: assign a `part` to check against templates. |
| LOADS_ABOVE_LIMIT | WARNING | validators | consumer | The loads one limit bounds sum above it; none is above it alone. | Lower the loads' summed draw below the limit, or split them across more limits. Write: nominal_current = "0.5 A" |
| LOAD_ABOVE_LIMIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A load's stated draw is above the limit that bounds it. | Lower the load's stated draw below its limit, or raise the source's limit. Write: nominal_current_a = "0.5" |
| MATES_DISABLED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A mate or harness line is refused in 0.22. | Use a cable. Write: d.cable("W1", P.CBL) |
| MATE_NOT_CONNECTOR | ERROR | validators | consumer | A mate end is not a connector or terminal (a relay coil, say). | Mate only connector or terminal functions. Write: d.mate(plug, connector) |
| MATE_PORT_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A mate's two functions have different port names, so some ports have no counterpart. | Mate two connectors whose port names match, so every port has a counterpart. Write: d.mate(j1, j2) |
| NET_ACROSS_UNIT_BOUNDARY_JOINED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A declared net joins pins in different units and no wire joins it, but every boundary pin has another way across; a net does not cross a unit boundary. | Join across the boundary with a wire, and keep nets inside one unit. Write: d.series(a, b, wire=...) |
| NET_ACROSS_UNIT_BOUNDARY_OPEN | ERROR | validators | consumer | A declared net joins pins in different units, no wire joins it, and a boundary pin has no other way across; a net does not cross a unit boundary. | Join across the boundary with a wire, and keep nets inside one unit. Write: d.series(a, b, wire=...) |
| NET_POTENTIAL_CONFLICT | ERROR | validators | consumer | One physical net joins two declared nets that are rails of different supply potentials. | No call clears this: remove the series that joins the two nets, or correct its ends. |
| NET_SHORTED | ERROR | validators | consumer | One physical net joins declared nets of different names. | No call clears this: remove the series that joins the two nets, or correct its ends. |
| NET_UNREALISED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A declared net's ports fall into more than one physical net, and no single board holds them all. Not for the PE net. | Put every port of the declared net on one board, or wire them into one net. Write: d.series(a, b) |
| ORDER_GROUP_DRAWS_NOTHING | ERROR | build | consumer | A `d.layout.order` hint names a group in which no function is drawn: its devices are drawn in another group (a series written there draws them there) or it holds none. The message names the group and where its members are drawn. | Order the group the message names as the one its members are drawn in, or drop the hint. Write: d.layout.order(run, lamps) |
| PE_NOT_GNYE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A single wire on a PE net is not green-yellow (an empty colour is not a finding). | Colour a PE wire green-yellow. Write: d.series(a, b, wire=(fr.colours.GNYE, 0.75)) |
| PE_PORT_OFF_PE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A port with role PE is on a net that is not PE. | Put a port with role PE on the PE net. Write: d.earth(*pins) |
| PLACEMENT_DUPLICATE | ERROR | validators | consumer | One item is placed more than once in the same aspect (function, location or product). | Place each item once in each aspect. Write: d.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", place="A1") |
| PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC binding's channel does not have the signal type the request asked for (or is not a declared channel at all). The message names the asked kind, the channel, its kind and both fixes. | Bind the request to a channel of the signal type it asked for. Write: K1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run") |
| PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC binding disagrees with the wiring: the request or channel function is wired to a different channel or request than its binding. | Wire the request to the channel its binding names, or change the binding. Write: K1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run") |
| PLC_CHANNEL_HAS_SETTINGS | ERROR | build | consumer | A device is wired to a PLC channel that carries its own settings (a name, routing, a scale or configured=False). | Wire the device to a channel without settings. Write: d.series(K1.coil, A1.do_2) |
| PLC_SIGNAL_NAME_TWICE | ERROR | validators | consumer | Two devices bound to one controller carry one signal name, so the CDP file would name two channels alike. | Rename one. Write: K1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run") |
| POTENTIAL_IN_TWO_SUPPLIES | ERROR | validators | consumer | One potential name is a rail of two differently named supplies. | Declare each rail name in one supply only. Write: d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")) |
| POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY | WARNING | validators | consumer | A net potential no supply declares: its pins get no rank and no power symbol. | Declare every net potential with a supply. Write: d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")) |
| RAIL_DUPLICATE_POTENTIAL | ERROR | validators | consumer | Two rail groups of one unit carry the same potential. | Flag one bridged group per potential in a unit. Write: x.run("24V", 4, bridged=True, rail=True) |
| RAIL_ON_FUSED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A rail group holds a terminal whose part has a protective link (a fuse in the path). | Flag the supply side of the fuse, not a fused terminal. Write: x.run("24V", 4, bridged=True, rail=True) |
| RAIL_WITHOUT_POTENTIAL | ERROR | validators | consumer | A rail group carries no power potential. | Declare the potential first, then flag the group. Write: d.dc_supply("S", plus=x[1], minus=y[1], voltage=24) |
| RATING_BREAKING_BELOW_FAULT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A protective device breaks less current than the prospective fault at its position. | Use a protective device that breaks more than the prospective fault current. Write: breaking_capacity = [{ nom = "15000 A", at = ["DC", "24 V"] }] |
| RATING_BREAKING_NO_DATA | WARNING | validators | consumer | A device states breaking points, but none covers the circuit voltage or time constant. | State a breaking point that covers the circuit voltage and time constant. Write: breaking_capacity = [{ nom = "15000 A", at = ["DC", "24 V", "10 ms"] }] |
| RATING_CURRENT_BELOW_BRANCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A function's rated current is below the current its branch can carry. | Use a function rated for the current its branch can carry. Write: current = [{ nom = "16 A", at = ["DC"] }] |
| RATING_CURRENT_KIND_UNSTATED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A function's part states a voltage rating for AC or for DC only, and the function stands on rails of the other current kind. | State the part's voltage rating for the current kind of its rails. Write: voltage = [{ nom = "24 V", at = ["DC"] }] |
| RATING_VOLTAGE_BELOW_CIRCUIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A function's rated voltage is below the voltage that stands across it. | Use a part rated for the voltage that stands across it. Write: voltage = [{ nom = "24 V", at = ["DC"] }] |
| REVISION_CURRENT_MISSING | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's (or the project's) current revision has no matching `Revision` history entry, so a title block prints no date. | Add a history entry for the current revision. Write: d.revision(1, date="2026-01-01", text="first", created="AB") |
| REVISION_DATE_FORMAT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A revision entry's date is not in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. | Write each revision date as YYYY-MM-DD. Write: d.revision(1, date="2026-01-01", text="first", created="AB") |
| REVISION_INITIALS_MISSING | ERROR | validators | consumer | A revision entry has no `created` (author initials). | Give each revision entry its author's initials in `created`. Write: d.revision(1, date="2026-01-01", text="first", created="AB") |
| SCALING_NOT_ANALOGUE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A function with an engineering range has no PLC request, or requests a DI, DO or RELAY channel. | Scale only an analogue channel: request it with fr.AI, fr.AO or fr.SignalType.RTD. Write: fn.plc(fr.AI, "level").scale("%", raw=(4, 20), eng=("0", "100")) |
| SCALING_RANGE_INVALID | ERROR | validators | consumer | A channel's engineering or raw range has its low value at or above its high value. | Write the low value first, below the high value. Write: fn.plc(fr.AI, "level").scale("%", raw=(4, 20), eng=("0", "100")) |
| SCREEN_DISABLED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable screen core is connected to a pin; screen connections are refused for now. | Leave the screen unconnected: the cable prints as shielded. Write: w1.core(fr.colours.BN, a, b) |
| STRIP_WITHOUT_TAG | ERROR | validators | consumer | A part-less top-level item, usually a floating strip, has no tag and no class code (no terminals, or disagreeing ones). | Give the strip a tag, a part, or terminals of one class code. Write: d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4) |
| SUPPLY_DIFFERS | ERROR | validators | consumer | Two declarations of one supply name disagree in current or rails. | Declare each supply name once, or twice with identical values. Write: d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")) |
| TERMINAL_MORE_THAN_TWO_PINS | ERROR | validators | consumer | A terminal has over two ports. | Use a two-pin part. Write: d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 2) |
| TERMINAL_POINT_OVERFILLED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A terminal point has more wires and cable cores than its part takes (conductors_per_clamp, default 1). | Use a part that takes more, or bridge a second terminal. Write: d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5-TWIN", 2) |
| UNIT_BOUNDARY_BYPASSED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A conductor or mate crosses out of a unit at a function that is not declared that unit's boundary. | Cross a unit's edge only at a function declared as its boundary. Write: d.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", interface=True) |
| UNIT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's parent chain loops back on itself. | Nest units as a tree, adding each unit once. Write: d.add(cabinet, "U1") |
| UNUSED_CONTRADICTED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A function declared unused is wired, or is a unit boundary connected across the unit the declaration is on. | Declare unused only a function that is wired nowhere, and for a boundary not across its unit. Write: d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P", interface=True, unused=True) |
| UNUSED_NOT_BOUNDARY | ERROR | validators | consumer | A point named in d.unused is no boundary point of its nested unit. | List in d.unused only the boundary points a nested unit offers; remove this one. Write: d.unused(pc.x3[3]) |
| UNUSED_POINT_WIRED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A boundary point or a port named in d.unused is wired. | Drop the pin from d.unused, or its wire; list an interface pin in the carrier, not the unit. Write: d.unused(pc.x3[4]) |
| WIRE_COLOUR_UNKNOWN | ERROR | validators | consumer | A wire or cable-product core colour is not a recognized IEC 60757 colour code (or combination). | Use an IEC 60757 code: a base code, two combined, a base with a core number, or SH. Write: d.series(a, b, wire=(fr.colours.BU, 0.75)) |
| WIRE_ON_TWO_HARNESSES | ERROR | validators | consumer | A wire joins plugs of two harnesses. | Keep each wire within one harness, or join the two harnesses through a cable. Write: d.pair(a, w1, b) |

---
