# Finding codes: build, release and library load

Codes the build, `release` and the library load emit when no model check names them. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items or unit instances under one parent print one designation: a tag equal to a sibling's text, or a retired or moved released one. | Give each item or unit instance under one parent its own tag, one no released revision reserved. Write: d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P") |
| DESIGNATION_MOVED | ERROR | release | consumer | An item or unit instance pinned in the previous release now prints a different designation, written or numbered. | No call clears this: restore the released tag on <subject>; only a new version may change it. |
| DESIGNATION_NEW_IN_REVISION | INFO | build, release | note | A new untagged item or unit instance took the next free number in a later revision. | Nothing is wrong; tag it if its number must stay fixed. |
| FILE_UNREADABLE | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file could not be read (missing file, permission error, or bad encoding). | No call clears this: fix the path, the file permissions or the UTF-8 encoding, then load again. |
| FLOAT_FORBIDDEN | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file has a bare TOML float, which the contract forbids (quote values as strings). | A number is a quoted string in a part file, never a bare TOML float. Write: nominal_current = "24.5 A" |
| HARNESS_END_AMBIGUOUS | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more ends of one cable print the same text in its drawing. | Give each cable end its own text with distinct locations or distinct tags. Write: d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P", place="A2") |
| MULTILINE_STRING | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file string contains a line break, which the contract forbids. | A string stays on one line; a line break is written as TOML's escaped `\n`. Write: description = "one line" |
| ORDER_HINT_CYCLE | ERROR | build | consumer | Authored `d.layout.order` hints contradict each other in a cycle (a before b, b before a), so no page order can honour them. | Drop one hint of the cycle the message names. Write: d.layout.order(a, b) for one direction only |
| PART_LIBRARY_VERSION_CONFLICT | ERROR | library load | consumer | Two `PartLibrary` records share a name but declare different versions. | Load one version of each named part library. Write: fr.design("demo-parts") |
| PLC_CHANNEL_CONTESTED | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more PLC requests of the channel's signal are wired to the same channel. The finding names the channel's pins and every request; none of them binds, and none goes to the free queue. | Keep one PLC request per channel and wire each other request to a channel of its own. Write: d.series(k1.coil["A1"], a1.di_1) |
| PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS | ERROR | build | consumer | A PLC request is wired so that several free channels of its signal tie: its net reaches them all, or all by a direct conductor. It gets no binding. | Wire the request straight to one channel of its signal, or free the other channels. Write: d.series(k1.coil["A1"], a1.di_1) |
| PLC_REQUEST_UNSERVABLE | ERROR | build | consumer | No free PLC channel of the requested signal type on the request's unit chain (its unit declares none, or every one is taken). | Add a PLC module with a free channel of the requested signal type to the unit or a parent unit, or move another request off one. Write: d.device("A1", "DEMO-PLC-DI-16") |
| PORT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more ports of one item print the same designation text, so a drawing or list cannot tell them apart. | Give each port of one item its own printed pin marking in the part file. Write: marking = "A2" |
| PRODUCT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items print the same product designation (location plus own label): both at one location or, unplaced, both unnumbered alike in one unit instance. | Give each item a distinct location or label: place one elsewhere, or tag it. Write: d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P", place="A2") |
| REFERENCE_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items in the function or location aspect print the same full reference designation (e.g. two unit instances at one location). | Place the two items at different locations so their designations differ. Write: d.device("X2", "DEMO-CONN-2P", place="A2") |
| TOML_INVALID | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file is not valid TOML. | The file is valid TOML: fix the syntax error the message names. Write: name = "value" |
| WIRE_ROW_UNRESOLVED | ERROR | build | consumer | A series or detail wire was written without a row, and at build end its net carries no rail of its unit, states no `source_row` and holds no PLC channel signal, or carries rails of two rows. The message names the net and the wire's two pins. | Give the wire a (colour, size), or a size with a row table; a rail never crosses a unit boundary. Write: d.series(a, b, wire=(fr.colours.BU, 0.75)) |

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-release/index.md -->

# Finding codes: build, release and verify

Codes the build, `release`, `verify` and the baseline check emit. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BASELINE_DIFFERS | ERROR | release, verify | consumer | A unit instance in the released subtree, or checked by `verify`, has a listing differing from its released baseline. | Bump the changed unit's revision and release it again, or restore its content. Write: fr.release(result, into, unit=<unit>) |
| BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED_NOTE | INFO | release, verify | consumer | A stored baseline cut before fransys 0.18.2 holds rows for a contact block that today's numbering cannot print; those rows were left out of the comparison and `verify` notes it. | Re-cut the stored baseline, which records its rows under today's rules. Write: fr.rebaseline(result, baselines, unit=<unit>) |
| BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED_REFUSED | ERROR | release, verify | consumer | A stored baseline cut before fransys 0.18.2 holds rows for a contact block that today's numbering cannot print; those rows were left out of the comparison and `release` of a unit nesting it refuses. | Re-cut the stored baseline, which records its rows under today's rules. Write: fr.rebaseline(result, baselines, unit=<unit>) |
| BASELINE_RULES_MOVED_NOTE | INFO | release, verify | consumer | A stored baseline's content is unchanged, but a later fransys prints its listing differently; `verify` notes it. | Re-cut the stored baseline under today's rules first. Write: fr.rebaseline(result, baselines, unit=<unit>) |
| BASELINE_RULES_MOVED_REFUSED | ERROR | release, verify | consumer | A stored baseline's content is unchanged, but a later fransys prints its listing differently; `release` of a unit nesting it refuses. | Re-cut the stored baseline under today's rules first. Write: fr.rebaseline(result, baselines, unit=<unit>) |
| BASELINE_TOO_OLD | ERROR | release, verify | consumer | A stored baseline was cut by a fransys older than the oldest release whose listing rules this build knows, or its manifest records no fransys version. | Verify with the fransys release that cut the baseline, or release a new revision. Write: fr.release(result, into, unit=<unit>) |
| EXPORT_NAME_CLASH | ERROR | build | consumer | Two different subjects (documents, items) would write to the same file name in `out_dir`. | Give <subject> or <other> a distinct name, location or fragment; a placement of a release is named by what `d.add` returned, which adds its tag to the PDF name. Write: fr.unit(<distinct name>, revision=<n>, interface_version=<n>, date=<date>, text=<text>, by=<by>) |
| INTERFACE_NOT_BUMPED | ERROR | release | consumer | The previous released revision of this unit (the highest below this one) has the same interface string but a different boundary. | Bump the interface version of <subject> if its boundary changed, or restore the previous boundary. Write: fr.unit(<name>, interface_version=<new>, ...) |
| RELEASE_FILE_CHANGED | ERROR | verify | consumer | A released file's hash differs, the folder holds a file its manifest omits, or the manifest does not parse. A CRLF-only change in a text file passes. | No call clears this: restore the file from version control; a released revision never changes. |
| RELEASE_FILE_MISSING | ERROR | verify | consumer | A file its manifest lists, or the manifest itself, is gone from a release folder. | No call clears this: restore it from version control. |
| RELEASE_HISTORY_UNRELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | A history entry after the first released one names a revision with no folder under `into`, in its own version. | Remove the entry from history=, or release that revision first. Write: fr.release(result, into, unit=<unit>) |
| RELEASE_NESTED_UNRELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | A unit anywhere in the subtree being released (not only direct children) has no baseline folder yet. | Release <subject> first, then release the containing unit. Write: fr.release(result, into, unit=<nested unit>) |
| RELEASE_NO_HISTORY | ERROR | release | consumer | The revision being released has no matching `Revision` history entry. | Add the missing entry: history= on fr.unit, or d.revision(...) for a system release. Write: fr.unit(<name>, ..., history=[<revision entry>]) |
| REVISION_ALREADY_RELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | The unit (or system) being released already has a baseline folder whose listing differs from the one to be written. | Bump the revision or version, or restore the frozen revision's content. Write: fr.unit(<name>, revision=<new revision>, ...) |
| SETTING_NEW_ENGINE_ONLY | WARNING | build | consumer | A settings file sets a `[font]` key. It applies to drawings from the new engine; the old engine, which draws every schematic today, keeps the built-in font until MODEL-TEXT, so this finding goes then. | Keep the key for the new engine's drawings, or remove it from the settings file. Write: fr.settings() |
| SHEET_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED | ERROR | build | consumer | A sheet record, or a unit's layout profile, uses a paper that is not A3 or A2 landscape. The supported formats are closed: a portrait sheet (height above width) and a sheet of any other size are refused. | Use a sheet of A3 or A2 landscape: take the default A3, or name A3 or A2 in the settings. Write: fr.settings(paper=...) |

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-render/index.md -->

# Finding codes: layout and render

Codes the layout and the drawing stage emit. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

A drawing set whose layout failed and drew nothing complete (PLACEMENT_PROBLEM, or an ERROR that stops its drawing) is not checked; every complete set is, and fr.write still refuses.

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ALIGN_DROPPED | WARNING | render | consumer | Symbols of a row group or a band rank, mated pins, or the legs of a trunk, cannot stand level because the stacks in their columns contradict it; layout dropped the alignment. | Shorten the stack, or move the members to the same end of their columns. Write: d.series(a, b, c) to stand a path in one column. |
| ANNEX_UNPLACED | WARNING | render | consumer | A tag, marking or table beside a symbol found no spot free of every outline, wire and text; it stands at its first spot, over what blocks it. | No call clears this: shorten the tag of <subject>, or move the symbols around it to leave a corner free. |
| BLOCK_NOT_PLACED | ERROR | render | Fransys | A block stands in no row of any page, or a whole block in more than one, so layout draws it by no rule; the message names the block and the stage. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| BOARD_NETS_NOT_DRAWN | ERROR | render | consumer | A board shares its unit with another top-level device, so layout draws it as a black box and drops the nets between its parts. | Make the board its own unit's only top-level device, with its parts as children. Write: @fr.unit(...) def board(d): b = d.device("A1", "DEMO-PCB-IO") and d.device("J1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", parent=b) in a unit of their own. |
| CARD_OVERFULL | INFO | render | note | The card of a box is wider than a page; the columns that do not fit stand free of the card on later pages. | Nothing is wrong; each such column is joined to its pin of <subject> by a drawn tag pair. |
| CHAIN_REFUSED | INFO | render | note | Boxes wired box to box do not make a chain that draws as one column: a ring, a box joined to three boxes, a box also wired by a trunk, or pins that do not face; or a box in parallel below another box, which has no layout yet. The message names the boxes and the hop that failed; the boxes are drawn unchained. | Nothing is wrong; the boxes are drawn unchained (rule CHAIN-COLUMN). |
| CONNECTION_DRAWN_TWICE | ERROR | render | Fransys | Two routes on one page join the same ports: the wires of a page close a loop. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN | ERROR | render | consumer | The drawn ports of one physical net do not lie in one drawn piece: a port no wire, dot, link or reference reaches, or two pieces with no reference pair between them. A group the model joins with a port off the document needs each drawn piece to end in a stub that names a port of the group outside it. | Give both ends a location so layout can route or cut them; check `layout.route`, `layout.symbol_placement` and `layout.page`. Wire the open end's function into a function block, or move its device into a unit. Write: d.series(a, b, ...) to draw it in its block. |
| CONNECTION_TO_UNDRAWN | WARNING | render | consumer | A connection, net group or rail has an end whose function layout never draws. | Put the missing end's item in a drawn unit or location, or remove the connection. Write: d.function(name, text) to place that item in a drawn group. |
| DANGLING_WIRE_END | ERROR | render | Fransys | A Fransys drawing defect: a drawn wire ends where no symbol port, junction dot, reference marker, other wire or joined bundle lane end stands. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP | ERROR | render | Fransys | Two boxes of a block diagram or of an overview view, or a tab and a box, overlap. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_CABLE_FANOUT | INFO | render | note | A cable reaches three or more boxes, so the block diagram draws a line from its first box to each other. | Nothing is wrong; split the cable only if a line per pair is not wanted. |
| DIAGRAM_CABLE_ONE_BOX | INFO | render | note | A cable's ends reach one box or none, so the block diagram draws no line for it. | Usually nothing to fix: the cable runs inside one box, or an end is an unmated plug. |
| DIAGRAM_LABEL_STRUCK | INFO | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view passes through a line label. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| DIAGRAM_LINES_SHARE_TRACK | INFO | render | Fransys | Two cables of a block diagram or an overview view run along one track. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX | ERROR | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view does not end on its box's outline or tab. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX | ERROR | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view crosses a box other than its own two. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_LOOSE_WIRE | INFO | render | note | In the system reading, a wire with no cable joins two boxes and is not drawn. | Usually nothing to fix: the unit pages show it as stubs. Put it in a cable to give it a line. |
| DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP | ERROR | render | Fransys | Two texts of a block diagram or an overview view overlap. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DOT_ON_CROSSING | ERROR | render | Fransys | A junction dot stands where two wires cross through each other, so the page shows them joined when they are not. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| DRAWING_SHORTS_NETS | ERROR | render | Fransys | The wires, junction dots and references of the drawings join ports of two physical nets, or a wire ends on another net's wire with no junction dot. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| DRAW_PROBLEM | ERROR | render | Fransys | A drawing set holds a record the renderer cannot draw, such as an unknown symbol key or an outline that is not a rectangle; the set draws no page. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the record and what the renderer expected. |
| FILL_UNDER_MIN | WARNING | render | consumer | A page is filled less than the minimum because no cut of the blocks fills it more. | Merge the group with its neighbour so the page fills. Write: d.function(name, text) to draw a device in the neighbour group. |
| FUNCTION_NOT_DRAWN | ERROR | render | consumer | A function of a connected set has no symbol (reason function_without_symbol), so the layout leaves it out of the drawing. The message names the function and the reason. | Give the function a part whose kind has a symbol. Write: d.device("K1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24") |
| FUNCTION_NOT_WIRED | WARNING | render | consumer | An undeclared function's symbol is on no net, so the page leaves it off (reason function_unwired). The message names the function. | Wire a pin of <subject> to another function, declare it spare, or remove it. Write: d.device("K1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24", unused=True) |
| HARNESS_WIRE_MISMATCH | ERROR | render | Fransys | A wire drawn in a cable or harness block page differs from the harness-wire row of the model: another core, other ends or another cable, or a row is not drawn once. The message names the cable, the core and the ends. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the cable and the core. |
| HEAD_OFF_LEGS | WARNING | render | consumer | A trunk is cut by a page and its head stands on the page with fewer of its legs. | Reorder the groups so the head and most of its legs share a page. Write: d.layout.order(a, b) with the head's group first. |
| LANE_WIRE_DROPPED | ERROR | render | consumer | Two consecutive cells of a lane have no pin facing each other, or a facing pin on no net, so no wire is drawn between them; the message names the cells. | Put the facing pins of <subject> and its neighbour on one net. Write: d.series(pin_a, pin_b). |
| MARKER_UNPAIRED | ERROR | render | Fransys | A reference marker is drawn and the marker it refers to is drawn on no page. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| MARKER_UNPLACED | WARNING | render | Fransys | A reference marker has no place inside the page: every level of its stagger leaves the content box, so layout draws no marker there; the message names its pin and page. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| MISSING_JUNCTION_DOT | ERROR | render | Fransys | Three or more ink directions meet at a wire end or vertex with no dot and no pin, so the page does not show the wires joined or apart. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| NET_NOT_DRAWN | ERROR | render | consumer | A net of two or more ends has under two drawn pins, so it is left out. A lone pin gives none. The message names the port. | Give the net a second drawn pin. Write: d.series(a, <subject>) |
| NOT_SERIES_PARALLEL | INFO | render | note | The named symbols are wired as a bridge, which no series or parallel holds. | Nothing is wrong; the symbols stay drawn, and CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN names each wire of the bridge left undrawn. |
| NO_BLOCK | ERROR | render | consumer | A box is drawn but belongs to no block, or to more than one, so layout places it by no rule; the message names it. | Wire <subject> to one function block, or remove it. Write: d.series(a, b, ...) to draw it in a block. |
| NO_CELL | WARNING | render | Fransys | A symbol is drawn but stands in no cell of any column, or in more cells than it has elements, so layout places it by no rule; the message names it. | No call clears this: report it with the smallest model that shows it. |
| ORDER_HINT_UNMET | WARNING | render | consumer | An authored order hint names two groups that are not on the same drawing set, so no page order can honour it. | Move both groups onto one drawing set, or drop the hint. Write: d.layout.order(a, b) for groups on one drawing set. |
| OUTLINE_NO_ROOM | WARNING | render | consumer | A nested unit stands on its parent's page, but its frame does not fit the page or would hold another unit's symbol; the unit is drawn with no frame. | Move the unit's devices together on the page, or give the unit its own page. Write: d.function(name, text) to place each device in one group. |
| OUT_OF_PAGE | WARNING | render | Fransys | A symbol body or a text lies outside the content box of its page. | No call clears this: report it with the smallest model that shows it. |
| OVERLAP | WARNING | render | Fransys | Two drawn boxes (symbol bodies, and symbols drawn at a pin end such as a power symbol), a text and a body, two texts, or a wire and a text meet on one page; the message names the first of them. | No call clears this: every fact is drawn and only the looks suffer. Report it with the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page and the members. |
| OVERVIEW_UNPLACED | ERROR | render | Fransys | The overview placer found no room plan for one view of the system overview, so the page would have no positions for it. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| PAGE_OVERFLOW | ERROR | render | consumer | A row of one block is taller than the page, so it stands on a page of its own. The message names the drawing set, the page and the devices standing in the row. | Split <block> into smaller function blocks, or use a taller sheet. Write: [paper] default = "A2" in the settings file, passed as fr.build(settings=fr.settings(path)) |
| PIN_MARKING_WRONG | ERROR | render | Fransys | A symbol prints at a pin a marking other than the one the model gives that port, or prints none where the port is marked, or one where it is not. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| PLACEMENT_PROBLEM | ERROR | render | Fransys | The placement core cannot take the design, or a set of it; the set draws no page. The message names the thing and what the core expected. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| POWER_SYMBOL_NOT_JOINED | ERROR | render | Fransys | A power symbol is drawn for a pin with no wire to it and not on the pin, so the page does not show the pin on its rail. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| RAIL_IDENTITY_SHARED | ERROR | render | consumer | Two unbonded nets of a cabinet print one rail identity (its flagged rail, else the cabinet plus the printed potential), so the page would join nets the model keeps apart. | No call clears this: two nets print one supply name with no protective device (fuse, breaker) between them, or the nearest device is not unique: put a fuse or breaker between them. |
| REFERENCE_OFF_DOCUMENT | WARNING | render | consumer | A printed reference points to a page that no page of its own document holds, and its text names no document, so a reader cannot tell which document to open. The message names the reference, its page and the target page. | Print both drawing sets in one document, or print the target's drawing set in a document so the reference names it. Write: fr.document(<preset>, <subject>, cover=<cover>) |
| ROUTE_WRONG_PORT | ERROR | render | Fransys | A wire of one lane ends on a port of one net and on a port of another net. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| SET_WITHOUT_PAGE | ERROR | render | consumer | A drawing set holds symbols but every net of them has its other end in another set, so the core path gives it no page. The message names the set. | Put the set's functions in the unit and location of the functions they are wired to. Write: d.device("K1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24", place="R") with the same place. |
| SPARE_FUNCTIONS | INFO | render | note | A function on no net, on an item that has other wired functions or declared `unused=`, is a spare: it is left off the schematic. One finding per document names the count and the items. | Nothing is wrong; wire the function if it is not a spare. |
| SPARE_TERMINALS | INFO | render | note | A terminal none of whose nets has a second end is a spare: it stands in the terminal list and is not drawn on the schematic. One finding per document names the count and the strips. | Nothing is wrong; wire the terminal if it is not a spare. |
| SYMBOL_PORT_MISSING | ERROR | render | consumer | A model port matches no port on its drawn symbol by any of the three binding rules. | Fix the part's port names, or map them with symbol_port keys. Write: symbol_port = 'in' on the port in the part file. |
| TAG_ACROSS_BODY | WARNING | render | consumer | A net joins a pin on one half of a generic box to a column of parts hung on its other half, so it is drawn as a tag pair, not a wire round the box (CROSS-HALF-TAGS). | Wire the parts to the box pins in one path. Write: d.series(<subject>, <other>) |
| TITLE_BLOCK_NOTICE_OVERFLOW | WARNING | render | consumer | The `notice` text passed to `fr.document(notice=)` does not fit the notice cell and would be cut. | Shorten the notice of <subject> to fit its cell. Write: fr.document(<preset>, <subject>, cover=<cover>, notice=<shorter notice>) |
| TITLE_BLOCK_NO_ROOM | WARNING | render | consumer | The sheet format's title-block band is under the required 20mm, or its title block is under the required 97.5mm wide. | Use a sheet format with a taller title-block band or a wider title block. Write: [paper] default = "A2" in the settings file, passed as fr.build(settings=fr.settings(path)) |
| TITLE_BLOCK_STACK_OVERLAP | ERROR | render | consumer | The profile's text height needs a taller title-block band than the sheet format has, so a title-block label overlaps its value. | Use a sheet format whose title-block band is at least the named height, or the house text height. Write: [paper] default = "A2" in the settings file, passed as fr.build(settings=fr.settings(path)) |
| TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW | WARNING | render | consumer | A one-line title-block field (title, number, customer, revision, date, author, page title, scope or sheet counter) does not fit its cell. | Shorten the field the message names. Write: d.project(title=<shorter text>, number=<number>, customer=<shorter text>, revision=<n>, author=<shorter text>) for the title, number, customer, revision or author, or d.function(<name>, <shorter text>) for a page title: the text of a block the page draws. |
| UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_KEY | ERROR | el | consumer | A function's chosen symbol key is not in the installed symbol library; it is drawn as a generic box. | Fix the symbol key of <subject> in its rule, choice or part data, or install a library version that has it. Write: symbol = '<symbol>' in the part file. |
| UNPRINTED_SET | ERROR | render | consumer | A drawing set has pages but no document prints it, so its items are not in any export. The message names the set and its items. | Add a document for the set's unit or location, passing its handle as the subject, or nest the unit in one that has one. Write: fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, cabinet, cover=cover) |
| WIDER_THAN_PAGE | ERROR | render | consumer | A row of columns is wider than the page even at its closest spacing. The message names the drawing set, the page and the devices standing in the row. | Shorten the row, lower the column count of the block, or raise the page width. Write: [paper] default = "A2" in the settings file, passed as fr.build(settings=fr.settings(path)). |
| WIRE_AS_REFERENCE | INFO | render | consumer | No orthogonal path on the wiring grid could be found for a connection, so it is drawn as a reference at its pin. | None needed: the connection is shown by its reference. To draw it as a wire, give its ports more room. |
| WIRE_MEETS_NET | WARNING | render | consumer | A fixed wire (a lane wire, join, trunk or drop) meets another net's wire and no detour exists, so it is drawn as placed; the message names the wire and its ends. | Move a symbol of <subject> or widen the gap beside it so the wire has a free path. Write: d.add(unit, tag) to move the device into a unit. |
| WIRE_NOT_ORTHOGONAL | ERROR | render | Fransys | A drawn wire has a segment that is neither horizontal nor vertical. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| WIRE_OVER_MARKER | WARNING | render | Fransys | A wire or a junction dot meets the box of a reference marker on one page, or a wire ends in it; the message names the first of them. | No call clears this: every fact is drawn and only the looks suffer. Report it with the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page and the members. |
| WIRE_OVER_PIN_TIP | ERROR | render | Fransys | A wire passes over the tip of a pin with its interior and no dot, so the page does not show whether it joins the pin. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. The message names the page. |
| WIRE_THROUGH_BODY | ERROR | render | consumer | A trunk is drawn through the drawn body of a symbol, or along its outline (a touch at a point or in its margin is not this error); the message names the net and the symbol. | No call clears this: send the smallest model that shows it. A wire never passes a symbol's body, so the model shows a drawing fault. |

# Finding codes: PDF

Codes the PDF output emits. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COVER_OVERFLOW | ERROR | write, release | consumer | A document's cover text plus revision table, measured by Typst at write, are taller than the content box; the write raises and writes nothing. | Shorten the cover file or the revision table of <subject>. Write: fr.document(<preset>, <subject>, cover=<shorter cover file>) |
| DOCUMENT_EMPTY_LIST | INFO | pdf | note | A document's list page (PLC, terminal, connector, wire-label, designation, cable or BOM) has no rows and is left out. | Usually nothing to fix (pdf-0019); add records to show it. |
| DOCUMENT_MIXED_SHEET_FORMATS | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A document's pages use more than one sheet format. | Give <subject> one sheet format for all its pages. Write: [paper] default = "A2" in the settings file, passed as fr.build(settings=fr.settings(path)) |
| DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A SCHEMATIC page has no drawing set and the document has no other content page, or a HARNESS_DRAWING or BLOCK_DIAGRAM page has no cable or diagram, or a drawing is missing, too large or not drawable yet: interleaved harness cables. | No call clears this: add the missing content to <subject> or shorten its texts. |
| DOCUMENT_NO_TOP_LEVEL_CABLES | INFO | pdf | note | A SYSTEM document's HARNESS_DRAWING section has nothing to draw: the model has no top-level cable. | Usually nothing to fix: add a top-level cable if one was expected. |
| DRAWING_SET_REPLICA_ONLY | INFO | pdf | note | A document's drawing set holds only black-box replicas of another unit's boundary. | Usually nothing to fix; add content if a page is intended. |
| MARKDOWN_UNSUPPORTED | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A document's cover or notes text uses a Markdown construct the PDF renderer does not support. | No call clears this: rewrite the cover or notes text of <subject> using only the supported Markdown subset. |
| TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING | WARNING | pdf | consumer | A unit document's unit has an empty `title` or `number`, so that title-block cell will print empty. | Give the unit release a title and a number. Write: fr.unit(<name>, title=<title>, number=<number>, ...) |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-kicad/index.md -->

# Finding codes: KiCad

Codes the KiCad import emits. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NET_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | kicad | consumer | Two or more KiCad netlist nets share a name, so KiCad would merge them on import. | No call clears this: rename one of the two supplies that share the name. |
| NET_SINGLE_PIN | INFO | kicad | note | A KiCad netlist net has one pin. | Nothing is wrong; wire a second end only if one was meant. |
| NODE_WITHOUT_COMPONENT | ERROR | kicad | consumer | A netlist pin belongs to an item with no footprint (or is the board's own pin), so KiCad drops it on import. | No call clears this: give the item's part a footprint, or model the connector as a child item with one. |
| PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS | ERROR | kicad | consumer | One component pad is in more than one KiCad netlist net. | No call clears this: fix the wiring so each pad is on exactly one net. |
| PART_WITHOUT_FOOTPRINT | WARNING | kicad | consumer | A board item's part has no footprint, so the KiCad netlist omits it. | No call clears this: add a footprint to the part's data. |
| PIN_ID_COLLISION | ERROR | kicad | part author | Two pins of one board part would write one KiCad pin id, because KiCad keys a pin by its name, which is the footprint pad name. A labelled connector may repeat a pin name in the drawing; the netlist cannot. | No call clears this: rename the part's pins so each is its footprint pad name, in the part file. |
| REFERENCE_DUPLICATE | ERROR | kicad | consumer | Two board parts share one reference designation in the KiCad netlist. | Give each part a distinct tag, which sets its designation. Write: d.device(<tag>, <mpn>) |
| UNCONNECTED_PIN | INFO | kicad | note | A pin of a board part is in no net in the KiCad netlist. | Usually nothing to fix unless a connection was meant. |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings-parts/index.md -->

# Finding codes: part files

Codes the part-file lint emits, at `fr.lint` and when `fr.design` or `fr.parts` loads a library. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BOARD_WITHOUT_PCB | WARNING | library load | part author | A part with `category = "board"` has no `[pcb]` table. | A board has a `[pcb]` table with a string `revision`, or a `category` other than board. Write: revision = "A" |
| CABLE_PAIR_INVALID | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[cable_product]` `pairs` entry breaks a pair rule: a core is out of range, in two pairs, or `SH`, or a `screen` is not a unique `SH` core. | Each `pairs` entry has two integer `cores` in range, neither `SH` nor in another pair, and a `screen` that is one unique `SH` core. Write: pairs = [{ cores = [1, 2], screen = 3 }] |
| CABLE_PRODUCT_CORE_COUNT | ERROR | library load | part author | A cable product's `core_count` differs from the number of its `core_colours`. | Make `core_count` equal the number of `core_colours`. Write: core_colours = ["BN", "BU"] |
| CABLE_WITHOUT_PRODUCT | ERROR | library load | part author | A part with `category = "cable"` has no `[cable_product]` table, or a part with another category has one. | A `category = "cable"` part has a `[cable_product]` table, and no other part does. Write: [cable_product] |
| CHANGEOVER_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link of a `contact_co` function joins two ports whose roles are not `common` with `break` or `make`. | Each `switched` link of a `contact_co` joins its `common` port to a `break` or `make` port. Write: links = [{ a = "11", b = "12", kind = "switched" }] |
| CHANGEOVER_ROLE | ERROR | library load | part author | A port of a `contact_co` function has a `role` other than `common`, `break` or `make`. | A `contact_co` port takes the role `common`, `break` or `make`. Write: role = "common" |
| CHANGEOVER_SYMBOL_PORT | ERROR | library load | part author | A port of a `contact_co` function sets `symbol_port`. | A `contact_co` port takes no `symbol_port`, since its throw roles bind the drawing. Write: { name = "12", role = "break" } |
| CLASS_CODE | ERROR | library load | part author | `class_code` is not 1 to 3 uppercase letters, starts with A, I or O, or starts with D, L, V, Y or Z. | Use 1 to 3 uppercase letters, the first as in IEC 81346-2, such as `K` or `QA`. Write: class_code = "K" |
| CONNECTOR_MARKING_REUSED | ERROR | library load | part author | Two connector functions of one part print the same label, their `marking` or else their `name`. | Each connector prints its own label, its `marking` or else its `name`. Write: marking = "X2" |
| CONTACT_WITHOUT_SWITCHED_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A `contact_no`, `contact_nc`, `contact_co` or `switch` function has no `switched` link in its `links`. | A contact or switch function has a `switched` link joining two of its ports, or a different `kind`. Write: links = [{ a = "1", b = "2", kind = "switched" }] |
| ENERGY_ON_NON_POWER | ERROR | library load | part author | A function whose `kind` is not `supply` or `load` sets `energy`. | Only a `supply` or `load` function takes `energy`. Write: kind = "load" |
| ENUM_VALUE | ERROR | library load | part author | A field typed as an enum holds a string that is no member of that enum. | The field takes one of the values the message lists, spelled as the contract gives them. Write: kind = "load" |
| FACET_KIND_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[function.connector]` sits on a function whose `kind` is not `connector`, or a `[function.plc_channel]` on one whose `kind` is not `plc_channel`. | A `[function.connector]` needs `kind = "connector"`, and a `[function.plc_channel]` needs `kind = "plc_channel"`. Write: kind = "connector" |
| FIELD_MISSING | ERROR | library load | part author | A required key is absent: the file's `schema`, its `[part]` table, or a required field of a table. | Each file needs `schema`, its `[part]` table and each required field, with values the contract allows. Write: schema = 2 |
| FIELD_TYPE | ERROR | library load | part author | A value has a TOML type the contract does not allow there, such as an integer for a quantity or a table where a list belongs. | Write the value as the type the message names, a quoted string for a rating or an integer for `schema`. Write: schema = 2 |
| FIELD_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A table holds a key the part-file contract does not name for that table. | A table takes only the keys the part-file contract names for it. Write: <contract key> = <same value> |
| FILE_NAME | WARNING | library load | part author | A part file's name has characters other than lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. | A part file name uses only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Write: relay-2co-24vdc.toml |
| FUNCTION_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `[[function]]` entries of one part have the same `name`. | Each `[[function]]` has its own `name`. Write: name = "co_3" |
| FUNCTION_WITHOUT_PORTS | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[[function]]` has an empty `ports` list. | A `[[function]]` lists at least one port in `ports`. Write: ports = [{ name = "1", role = "generic" }] |
| JOIN_INTO_CONNECTOR | ERROR | library load | part author | A header pin's `joins` names a port of a `connector` function. | A header pin `joins` a port of a non-connector function of the same part. Write: joins = "k1.A1" |
| JOIN_PORT_TWICE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two header pins of one part both `joins` the same function port. | Each function port is joined by at most one header pin. Write: joins = "k1.A2" |
| JOIN_PORT_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A header pin's `joins` value does not name a port of a function in this part, or is not `<function>.<port>`. | `joins` is `<function>.<port>`, naming a port of another function of this part. Write: joins = "k1.A1" |
| LIBRARY_FILE_MISSING | ERROR | library load | part author | The library root has no `library.toml` file. | The library root holds a `library.toml` with `schema`, `name` and `version`. Write: schema = 2 |
| LINK_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `links` entries of one function join the same pair of ports, in either order. | Each pair of ports is linked once in a function, in either order. Write: links = [{ a = "11", b = "12", kind = "switched" }] |
| LINK_PORT_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A `links` entry's `a` or `b` is not a `name` in the function's `ports`. | Each `a` and `b` names a port listed in `ports`. Write: a = "11" |
| LINK_SELF | ERROR | library load | part author | A `links` entry has the same port as `a` and `b`. | `a` and `b` name two different ports. Write: b = "12" |
| PART_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two part files declare the same `manufacturer` and `mpn` pair. | Each `manufacturer` and `mpn` pair is declared by one part file only. Write: mpn = "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24" |
| PART_SCHEMA_OLD | ERROR | library load | part author | A part file or `library.toml` is written in schema 1. | Run `python -m fransys migrate-parts DIR` on the library folder; it rewrites each schema 1 file to schema 2. Write: schema = 2 |
| PINCOUNT | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[function.connector]` has a `pincount` below 1. | A connector `pincount` is an integer of 1 or more. Write: pincount = 2 |
| PLC_CHANNEL_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `[function.plc_channel]` tables of one part have the same `channel` and `signal`. | Each `[function.plc_channel]` has its own `channel` and `signal`. Write: channel = 4 |
| PORT_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two ports of one function have the same `name`. | Each port of one function has its own `name`. Write: name = "A2" |
| PORT_NAME_SHARED | ERROR | library load | part author | Two functions of one part give a port the same name, and their printed designations would be the same. | Each port name is unique across the part, so the printed designations differ. Write: name = "A3" |
| POWER_LOSS_TWICE | ERROR | library load | part author | `power_loss` is set both in the part's `[rating]` and in a function's `[function.rating]`. | `power_loss` is stated once, in `[rating]` or in one `[function.rating]`. Write: power_loss = { nom = "2.5 W" } |
| PROTECTION_LINK_KIND | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link sits on a `protection` function, or a through link's `kind` does not fit its protection `type`. | A fuse, mcb, motor_breaker or rcd link is `protective`, an overload link is `conductive`, never `switched`. Write: kind = "protective" |
| PROTECTION_TYPE_ON_NON_PROTECTION | ERROR | library load | part author | A function whose `kind` is not `protection` has a `[function.block]` table with a `type`. | Only a `protection` function has a `[function.block]` table with a `type`. Write: kind = "protection" |
| PROTECTION_WITHOUT_TYPE | WARNING | library load | part author | A `protection` function has no `type` in its `[function.block]` table. | `[function.block]` needs a `type`: fuse, mcb, motor_breaker, overload or rcd. Write: type = "mcb" |
| RATING_TABLE_EMPTY | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[rating]`, `[function.rating]` or `[function.operating]` table has no field. | A rating table holds at least one value, or the table is deleted. Write: voltage = [{ nom = "24 V", at = ["DC"] }] |
| RATING_VALUE_INVALID | ERROR | library load | part author | A figure or quantity is not written as schema 2 asks: a quantity is a number, a space and a unit symbol, and a figure an inline table. | Write each quantity as a string such as "24 V", above zero in a rating, and each figure as an inline table. Write: voltage = [{ nom = "24 V", at = ["DC"] }] |
| REST_DISAGREES_WITH_KIND | ERROR | library load | part author | A switched link's `rest` disagrees with its function's `kind`: `contact_no` is open at rest, `contact_nc` is closed. | `rest` is `open` for `contact_no` and `closed` for `contact_nc`, or change `kind`. Write: rest = "open" |
| REST_ON_UNSWITCHED_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A link whose `kind` is not `switched` sets `rest`. | Only a `switched` link takes `rest`. Write: kind = "switched" |
| SCHEMA_MIXED | ERROR | library load | part author | A part file's `schema` differs from the `schema` in its library's `library.toml`. | The file's `schema` is the value `library.toml` names, or both change in one commit. Write: schema = 2 |
| SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED | ERROR | library load | part author | A `schema` value is not in `SUPPORTED_SCHEMAS`, which today holds only 2. | The `schema` is an integer in the supported set, only 2 today. Write: schema = 2 |
| SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link of a `switch` or `generic` function sets no `rest`. | A `switched` link of a `switch` or `generic` function states its `rest`. Write: rest = "open" |
| SYMBOL_PORT_WITHOUT_SYMBOL | ERROR | library load | part author | A port sets `symbol_port`, but its function has no `symbol`. | A port with `symbol_port` needs its function to have a `symbol`. Write: symbol = "operating-device" |
| SYMBOL_REST_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A function's `symbol` implies a rest state (`make-contact` open; `break-contact` and `emergency-stop` closed), and its switched links, stated or implied by its `kind`, are all at the other one. | The symbol and the switched links agree on one rest state: make-contact is open, break-contact and emergency-stop are closed. Write: rest = "open" |
| SYMBOL_SLUG | ERROR | library load | part author | A function's `symbol` is not a lowercase, hyphenated slug. | `symbol` is lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, such as `change-over-contact`. Write: symbol = "change-over-contact" |
| SYMBOL_TYPE_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A protection function's `symbol` is `fuse` or `circuit-breaker`, but its protection `type` is another one. | A `fuse` symbol needs `type = "fuse"`, a `circuit-breaker` symbol needs `type = "mcb"`. Write: type = "fuse" |
| TABLE_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | The file has a top-level table that is neither `schema` nor a part-file table the contract names. | A top-level table is `schema` or a table the part-file contract names. Write: [part] |

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/examples/index.md -->

# Examples

Worked examples of whole circuits, each shown the easy way and the efficient way, and a pointer to
a full build script outside this repository. All parts are from `demo_parts`.

## A motor starter with a start/stop latch

S1 and S2 are two contact blocks: S1's break contact (`nc`) stops, S2's make contact (`no`) starts.
The power circuit runs from the three-phase supply through a breaker, the contactor's make
contacts (`main`) and an overload relay to a terminal strip. A cable carries it to the motor. The
power supply G1 takes its mains from L1 and N of the same supply. The control circuit runs from the 24 V rail through
the stop contact, a latch and the overload's break contact to the contactor coil. The latch is the
start contact in parallel with the contactor's own
auxiliary make contact.

`d.series(a, b, ...)` is the one spelling for a chain of connections, and `d.parallel(...)` puts
branches between two neighbours. The design is a plain top design: no place and no cabinet.

```python
# easy: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5-TWIN")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", x0[1], x0[2], x0[3], n=x0[4])
g1 = d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", g1)
q0 = d.device("Q0", "DEMO-MCB-3P")
q1 = d.device("Q1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")
f1 = d.device("F1", "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P")
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
s2 = d.device("S2", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, q0.element, q1.main, f1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, g1.input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(dc.plus, s1.nc, d.parallel(s2.no, q1.aux), f1.aux, q1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

The efficient version builds the same model. The devices come from one table of tag and part
number, so adding a device is one more line in the table.

```python
# efficient: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

PARTS = {
    "G1": "DEMO-PSU-24",
    "Q0": "DEMO-MCB-3P",
    "Q1": "DEMO-CTR-3P-24",
    "F1": "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P",
    "S1": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
    "S2": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
}

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5-TWIN")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)), n=x0[4])
i = {tag: d.device(tag, mpn) for tag, mpn in PARTS.items()}
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", i["G1"])
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, i["Q0"].element, i["Q1"].main, i["F1"].main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, i["G1"].input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
latch = d.parallel(i["S2"].no, i["Q1"].aux)
d.series(dc.plus, i["S1"].nc, latch, i["F1"].aux, i["Q1"].coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

## Sixteen sensors to a terminal strip

Each sensor is one device, wired by its other pin to the 24 V rail and by its signal pin to its own terminal on a strip. The strip
takes its terminals in number order: each series that names the strip takes the next free one.
A series from the rail through a sensor's function to the strip wires its load pin `B` to that terminal. The first
sensor added lands on terminal 1, so the sensors are added from B16 down to B1.

```python
# easy: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    b16 = d.device("B16", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b16.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b15 = d.device("B15", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b15.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b14 = d.device("B14", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b14.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b13 = d.device("B13", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b13.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b12 = d.device("B12", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b12.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b11 = d.device("B11", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b11.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b10 = d.device("B10", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b10.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b9 = d.device("B9", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b9.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b8 = d.device("B8", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b8.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b7 = d.device("B7", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b7.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b6 = d.device("B6", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b6.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b5 = d.device("B5", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b5.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b4 = d.device("B4", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b4.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b3 = d.device("B3", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b3.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b2 = d.device("B2", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b2.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b1 = d.device("B1", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(dc.plus, b1.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

The efficient version is a list of sensor tags in the order the strip hands out terminals, and one
loop.

```python
# efficient: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

SENSORS = [f"B{n}" for n in range(16, 0, -1)]

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24"))
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    for tag in SENSORS:
        sensor = d.device(tag, "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
        d.series(dc.plus, sensor.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

## One full cabinet

`examples/demo-skid` is one whole cabinet on demo parts: terminal strips with rails, a PLC with its
channels, and fans and valves wired through them. Read it in this order:

1. `examples/demo-skid/README.md`: what the skid holds and how to load it.
2. `examples/demo-skid/skid.py`: `supply`, `starters`, `valves`, then the `skid` unit that joins them.
   `design()` adds the unit as `U1` to a cabinet.

The skid has no cable. For a cable, read the motor starter above and series.md, Cables.

## The whole shape of a build script

The examples above build small pieces of a design. For a real build script end to end, see
`examples/pump-station/build.py` in the public `fransys` repository, at the tag you pinned. It has its
own parts library (`example_parts`), so it cannot run as a block on
this page. It shows:

- The project and its revision history, set up once at the top.
- A cabinet unit with a second unit, the relay-interface board, mated to it through headers.
- Locations and functions built section by section: incoming supply, control supply, a PLC rack,
  and a per-pump circuit written once as a function and called for each pump.
- Several documents for several audiences from one design, then one `fr.build` and a `fr.write`
  per audience.

Consumer bugs become permanent tests in `tests/field_cases/` of the Fransys repository. Each
module's docstring states the engineering shape and the decision that fixed it.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-0.6/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.6

This page lists every change a 0.5 consumer script or part file must make for 0.6.
Each entry gives the 0.5 spelling, the 0.6 spelling and one line of why.
The 0.5 spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

## Imports and build

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.author` and `from fransys.author import ...` | `d = fr.design("demo_parts", place="C1")`, then calls on `d` | `fransys.author` left `__all__`: the engineer surface is the one spelling. |
| `fr.build(parts, d.draft())` | `fr.build(d)` | A design holds its library, so the build needs no second argument. |
| `fr.build(parts, d.draft(), doc)` | `fr.build(d, doc)` | The same reason, with a document. |

Pass `fr.design` the generated parts module or the import-name strings that `fr.parts` takes.

## Tags and units

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `location("-C1")`, `"=M1"`, `"+X1"` | `d.location("C1", text)` | A tag is a bare key. A prefixed tag raises. |
| `unit("-A1", ...)` | `@fr.unit("A1", ...)` | A unit name is a key, with no `-`, `+` or `=` prefix. |
| unit release `interface=` | `interface_version=`; boundary values are `fn.limits(...)` | `interface` now means only the boundary marking, `interface=True`. |
| `d.add(fn, "io")`, the second argument a lowercase key | `d.add(fn, "U1")`, a printed tag | The argument is the instance's tag and key, and a container prints it: `-U1-J1`. A lowercase letter raises. |
| `d.location` called twice for one tag, order mattering | one call per tag, in any order | A location is order-free, and its text is set once. |

## Devices and terminal strips

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `item(mpn, tag=, at=, group=)` | `d.device("Q1", mpn, place=)` | The electrotechnical word is device, and its tag is the first argument. |
| `strip.terminal(3)` | `X1[3]` | A terminal strip is indexed by terminal number. |
| `strip.take(...)` | `X1[3]` or `X1.run(label, n)` | `take` had no surface spelling. Indexing and runs cover it. |
| `bridge(t1, t2)` | `X1.run(label, n, bridged=True)` | A bridge joins the adjacent terminals of one run. A run may be two terminals. |
| two parts of one MPN in a library | no surface spelling | The surface names a part by its MPN, which then names both makers. |

`d.device` and `d.terminal_strip` raise on such an MPN and name both makers.
The surface has no spelling for either part. Report the case, as a consumer case brings a form back.

## Wires

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Wire(colour, mm2, label)` | `wire=(BU, 0.75)` and `d.wire(a, b, label="L1")` | `Wire` is gone. The tuple is the one form, and the label belongs to the call. |
| `wiring(a, b, n=2)` | `d.wire(a, b, n=2)` | One spelling for a wire between two pins. |

## Groups, supplies and ids

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a terminal's `group` argument, `d.interface(fn, ...)` | the `d.function` block where the terminal is first taken; `X1.x1.limits(rating=, operating=)` | One spelling each: the block names the group, and `interface` means the boundary marking. |
| a supply with no source device | `d.dc_supply(name, plus=, minus=, voltage=)` | The pins and the voltage stand in for the source. |
| a DC supply's M rail named `M` | the rail is named `0V` | The 0 V conductor carries its potential as its name. |
| `derive.unit_ids(model)` | `sorted(fr.derive.units(model))` | It listed the keys of the units table. |
| a unit function returning a dict, `d.add(...)` returning `AddedUnit` | a `typing.NamedTuple` instance, returned by `d.add` as it is | A misspelt boundary is a type error. `fr.Run` and `fr.Terminal` type the fields that hold strips, runs and terminals. |
| `Design.unit_id` | a unit is named by its release name: `unit="pump-cabinet"` in `fr.write`, `fr.release`, `fr.verify` | There is no successor; the release name is the one name. |
| `derive.wire_label_rows` | `derive.wire_rows` and `<set>-wires.csv` | WIRE-LIST removed it on purpose (bf2d3968). |
| a per-terminal part on a strip | one strip part; a run labelled `"PE"` takes `pe=` | The strip has no per-terminal part. |

## Findings that change

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Net.potential` with no supply declared | declare the supply system: `d.ac_supply(...)` or `d.dc_supply(...)` | Without it the model gets POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY (WARNING) and no rank. |
| `Profile.potential_ranks` | removed: ranks follow the declared supply | A rank keyed by rail name left a rail named `L` or `12V` unranked, and its pins swapped sides. |

## Part files

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a switched link with no `rest` | `rest = "open"` or `rest = "closed"` | SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST is an ERROR. |
| `conductor = "PE"` on a pin | `role = "pe"` | A PE pin is named by its role. The pole-side `conductor` value is refused. |
| a protection `type` on a non-protection function | remove the `type` | A load ERROR in 0.6. |

A changeover contact (`contact_co`) needs no `rest` line.
Its throw roles imply it: `break` is closed at rest and `make` is open.
Its ports must still carry `common`, `break` and `make`, as in 0.5.
Only `switch` and `generic` functions with a switched link need `rest`.

## Stored models

The model `SCHEMA_VERSION` went from 2 to 7. Rebuild every stored model with `fr.build`.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/kicad/index.md -->

# KiCad

Fransys writes a KiCad netlist for each board in your model. This page shows how to import it into a
KiCad 9 board, which settings to use, and how to start a part file from a KiCad symbol.

The model is the schematic. Use KiCad for the board only: no KiCad schematic file, and no
"Update PCB from Schematic". The board gets its parts and nets from the netlist, through the PCB
editor's File > Import > Netlist. The import is a manual step.

## Get the netlist

`fr.write(result, out_dir, intermediates=...)` writes one netlist per board into the
intermediates folder, named `netlist-<board>.net`. A netlist is not an export, so it never lands in `out_dir`.

`fr.check(result)` reports the KiCad findings. Read them first. An `ERROR` (`REFERENCE_DUPLICATE`,
`NET_NAME_DUPLICATE`, `PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS`, `PIN_ID_COLLISION`) means do not import yet. Each code is in findings-kicad.md.

### Pin names and pads

A labelled connector function may repeat a pin name: the drawing prints `-B1-Main:1` and `-B1-Voltage:1`, so the label is not the KiCad pin. KiCad keys a pin by its name, which is the footprint pad name, so it needs each pin name unique per part. When two pins of one part would write the same KiCad pin id, `PIN_ID_COLLISION` is an `ERROR`, wired or not. Rename the part's pins so each is its footprint pad name.

## Import settings

Open File > Import > Netlist in the PCB editor, pick the file, and set the dialog like this.

| Setting | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Link Method | Link footprints using component tstamps (unique ids) | Each part's id comes from the model, not from its designation. A renumbered part (`R1` becomes `R7`) keeps its footprint, position and routing. |
| Delete footprints with no components in netlist | On | The model decides what is on the board. A part you remove from the model leaves the board. |
| Replace footprints with those specified in netlist | On | The footprint comes from the part file. A footprint changed by hand on the board is drift. |
| Delete/replace footprints even if locked | Off | A lock is a deliberate choice. The import reports the locked footprint, and you resolve it by hand. |
| Delete tracks shorting multiple nets | Off | It silently removes routing. Run DRC after the import and fix reported shorts by hand. |

Never switch the link method on a board that already has footprints. Footprints imported by
reference designator carry no matching ids, so a later import by id sees every part as new.

## Import steps

1. Build the project and write it, so the netlist is current.
2. Read the KiCad findings and fix every `ERROR`.
3. In the PCB editor, open File > Import > Netlist, pick the file, and set the settings above.
4. Click **Load and Test Netlist** first. It is a dry run. Read "Changes to Be Applied" and check that
   the deletions and replacements are the ones you expect. Errors must be 0.
5. Click **Update PCB**, place the new footprints, and route.
6. Run DRC. Commit the board file together with the model change that caused it.

## Footprints that only exist on the board

Mounting holes, fiducials and logos have no part in the model. Set the footprint attribute
**Not in schematic** on each one, in its footprint properties. KiCad then leaves them alone
when "Delete footprints with no components in netlist" is on.

## Parts that are not installed

A part with `installed = False` stays in the netlist and on the board, marked do-not-populate.
The BOM report leaves it out. You do not remove it from the board.

## Start a part file from a KiCad symbol

`python -m fransys_kicad <file.kicad_sym> <symbol>` reads one symbol's pins from a `.kicad_sym`
library and prints a part-file skeleton to stdout. It has one `[[function]]` of kind `generic`, with
one port per pin.

```text
uv run python -m fransys_kicad my-library.kicad_sym DEMO-RLY-2U > parts/demo-rly-2u.toml
```

Open the new file and fill in `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `category` and `class_code`
under `[part]`. Each is an empty string marked `# TODO`. Then run `fr.lint` over the library
(see parts.md). The skeleton lints clean once those five fields are filled.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.23.5/guide/moving-to-fransys/index.md -->

# Moving to Fransys

This page lists every change a script written for version 0.6.1 under the old name must make for Fransys 0.7.0.
Each entry gives the old spelling, the new one and one line of why.
The old spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

## Import and alias

```text
import schematika as sk
from schematika.colours import BU
```

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.device("Q1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
model = fr.build(d)
```

Every `sk.` call becomes `fr.` with the same name and arguments. The distribution and the import
name are both `fransys` now, so no `schematika` module remains.

## The pin line

```text
schematika @ git+<the old repository>@v0.6.1#subdirectory=packages/schematika
```

```text
fransys @ git+https://github.com/OleJBondahl/fransys@v0.7.0#subdirectory=packages/fransys
```

Pin the exact tag, as before. The repository is the public one, and the subdirectory is the
`fransys` package.

## The parts module command

| old | new |
|---|---|
| `python -m schematika parts-module` | `python -m fransys parts-module` |

The arguments are the same. Regenerate the parts module with the new command, then rebuild.
The generated file records the library's digest, which the rename does not change.

## The intermediates folder

| old | new |
|---|---|
| `.schematika/` | `.fransys/` |

Per-page SVGs and other intermediates go to `.fransys/`. Replace the `.schematika/` line in your
`.gitignore` with this one.

```text
.fransys/
```

Stored baselines verify unchanged: the rename moves no listing text.
